description: Objective:To develop a unified and traceable data management system that enables the consistent integration of data,simulation models, and tools related to digital twin spacecraft across multiple disciplines, mission phases, and mission types. The solution shall be based on the Space System Ontology (SSO) for its semantics yet shall allow for flexibility in the mapping towards different sources and authoring tools.Description:The digital twin spacecrafts represent virtual representations of the spacecraft throughout the project lifecycle with synchronised interaction means. Examples are the digital twin spacecraft "as designed", "as built" but also "as operated". The data and information into (and out of) these digital twins come from the underlying digital spacecraft context, a federated set of databases and system information systems that capture all thespacecraft data and knowledge available. Within this eco-system, comprising and supporting variousstakeholders with different roles, digital continuity refers to the consistent andtraceable integration of data,models, and simulation tools across different disciplines, mission phases, and even across differentmissions.This means that all the data, simulation models and discipline-specific tools are reusable and interoperablethroughout the entire spacecraft lifecyclefrom early design through to operations. More specifically it includes the mapping of the lifecycle usage of models and data and defining how simulation assets contribute to various phases and ensuring their continuous integration. The simulation artefacts include the mission scenarios as input to the test scenarios and time-series data as output of the simulation and AIV test campaigns. Within the RatioSim community already a system-level simulator reference architecture exists that serves as a basis.Within ongoing Digital Twin Spacecraft activities an overview is created of the spacecraft data fromrequirements to mission/system design, up to PLM and CAD data. The SSO defines the semantics of the dataand the domain specific concepts. By taking theOverall Semantic Modelling for Space Systems Engineering(OSMoSE) methodology, the generation of the information system in line with the data and semantics isensured and to large extent automated.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Analysis of the lessons learned, including:- Formal semantic approach of space system ontology and OSMoSE for overall semantic interoperability,- RatioSim system level simulator reference architecture, specifying the ecosystem, specification,development and usage of any systemlevel simulator as basis for digital twins.- Use-cases and data specifics coming from pilot digital twin activity. This includes the different roles ofdifferent stakeholders.- Digital twin spacecraft and digital spacecraft data management aspects.- High levelarchitecture definition of data management system supporting the digital twin spacecrafts.- Definition of methodology to define the semantics of the data into space system ontology model (top downand bottom-up approach, allowing for configuration and flexibility).- Development of the data management system, following the OSMoSE guidelines for generation of theinformation system based on the created SSO.- Testing and verification of the developed system using real-life data/simulators for a number of digital twinuse-cases.Deliverables: Prototype, Report, Software
title: DIGITAL CONTINUITY FOR DIGITAL SPACECRAFT AND DIGITAL TWIN SPACECRAFTS - EXPRO+

description: Objective: To develop innovative end-to-end payload system architectures, techniques and algorithms enabling large distributed arrays for PNT based on high-gain beamforming.Description: Large arrays of antennas and distributed arrays of antennas are being considered for the generation of very high-gain beamforming. In this case, the main objective is to achieve a high received power by the ground user receivers, such that high data rates can be supported per user. Large and distributed arrays can be considered for PNT, both for Earth and Spaced Service Volume users and applications. One clear expected advantage would be to achieve much larger received power on the user receivers than with current GNSS systems. This can be of interest in particular in harsh propagation conditions, including the presence of interference and jamming, or to reach very far-away space users/assets. The objective of this activity is to design techniques and algorithms to enable large distributed array satellite and payload (PL) system architectures/configurations for PNT. The focus will be on the generation of very high-gain beamforming, while ensuring the transmission of high-accuracy signals-in-space, even when wide-band signals are used. Both the transmission in L-band (reference) and alternative bands (e.g., S and Cbands) will be addressed. Additionally, the activity will investigate innovative ideas for the exploitation of the large distributedarray architecture for PNT purposes, leveraging concepts and operational modes exploited in other space applications like SyntheticAperture Radar (SAR) systems. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition and design of innovative techniques and algorithms in the areas identified above; - Implementation of the required tools/software enabling the assessment of the proposed techniques and algorithms; - Assessment/test of the different techniques and algorithms in simulated conditions; - Identification of themost promising techniques/algorithms based on the results obtained; - Definition of the proposed the way-forward to further matureeach of the promising techniques/algorithms identified.Deliverables: Report, SoftwareProcurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSI is requested. title: DISTRIBUTED ARRAY END-TO-END PAYLOAD SYSTEM ARCHITECTURES FOR PNT - EXPRO+

description: ObjectivesTo increase the efficiency of photobioreactors by an improved design of light conduction anddiffusion inside the reactor.DescriptionThe need for regenerative life support systems for long term space missions necessitates a questfor increased efficiency of Photobioreactors. The light intensification of photobioreactors is animportant building block to increase the return on investment with respect to light energy introducedvs oxygen yield in a defined volume.Previous activities have identified as a priority the need to progress on specific technologies, suchas the type of light sources and on innovative materials for light conductionand diffusion (e.g.polymers, leaking rods, specific optical fibers, lightning fabrics). This activity attempts to push theboundaries of photobioractor efficiency even further (compared to BIORAT-1) by investigating amore efficient light diffusion and as well characterization of the impact on the process and thebiomass.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review the state of the art for light intensified photobioreactiors and energy efficient lightguidance systems- Design a test bench with realistic operational parameters (light, flow, active species etc.)and test the most optimal configuration to achieve best possible efficiency w.r.t. volumetricoxygen and biomass production- Assess the potential biological effects of immersed light sources and possiblecountermeasures against fouling and clogging- Provide a development plan for operational hardware on ground and in space includingMAIT aspects for an operational scenario and define the scaling laws.Procurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSI is requested. title: LIGHT CONDUCTION AND DIFFUSION MATERIALS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF LIGHT INTENSIFIED PHOTOBIOREACTORS

description: To advance hybrid manufacturing strategies that integrate conventional and advanced techniques to enhance the performance, functionality and competitiveness of space hardware.Description:Hybrid manufacturing combines subtractive methods (e.g. milling, turning,grinding) with additive processes(e.g. powder bed processes, direct energy deposition). It may also include fabrication/joining steps like welding,bonding or brazing. This approach aims to overcome limitations of individual processes, enabling theproduction ofhigh-performance, competitive components. Such methodologies are of growing relevance particularly in propulsion, thermal management and structural systems. The key drivers include:- Geometric complexity: enabling the manufacture of intricate, topology-optimisedstructures difficult to realiseby conventional means alone.- Material efficiency: by adding material only where needed, hybrid manufacturing reduces waste and optimizes material usage.- Functional performance: enabling graded material properties, local reinforcements or tailored functionality.- Cost and lead time: consolidating steps, minimising waste and enabling complex geometries, though it mayrequire specialised planning, equipment and qualification.- Design flexibility: greater customization and flexibility in design, making it ideal for producing bespoke or low volume parts.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Survey of relevant techniques, materials and equipment capabilities relevant to a hybrid manufacturing approach.- Selection of two representative case studies with associated requirements (e.g. one propulsion component, one thermal management part).- Design and definition of the hybrid manufacturing route for each case study.- Manufacturing and functional testing of demonstrators. The utilisation of new digital methods for supportinghybrid manufacturing decisions is welcomed. This may include artificial intelligence techniques, such asdeep/federated learning techniques, as well as a focus on use-cases of generatively designed parts (whichinherently benefit from the hybrid manufacturing techniques), alongside the artificial intelligence and machine learning data-driven learning.- Economic analysis, including cost comparison with conventional approaches and life-cycle considerations.Deliverables: Breadboard, ReportNOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.
title: HYBRID MANUFACTURING FOR SPACE APPLICATION - EXPRO PLUS

description: To assess the potential use of alternative insulating materials (e.g. aerogel) to improve the thermal performance of classical MLI,and sustaining the extreme environments applicable to L4 Enceladus Lander.Current thermal insulation solutions for Solar System missions are mainly based onconductive and radiative insulation (e.g. JUICE Nomex reinforced MLI), or includeconvective insulation function, not assessed for L4 Enceladus Lander environments (e.g.ExoMars Upilex foam). Due to the L4 Lander extreme environment on Enceladus (lowtemperatures, potential interaction with plumes, snow and/or ice and challenging landingconditions), the use of classical MLI technology, even with an efficient, reinforced designsuch as the one used in JUICE, is probably insufficient to achieve the required thermalinsulation and reduce the use of electrical heating. Heaters use is to be minimized (with atarget of 0 W), as the electrical power consumption is directly linked to the mass andlifetime span of the Lander on Enceladus surface. In addition, the selected thermal controltechnologies shall ensure nominal performance while keeping physical integrity (stringentmechanical loads during landing) and fulfilling mass, EMC, planetary protection and otherrequirements of the mission.Potential technologies such as Aerogel have been identified in similar missions such asMars Pathfinder ("(...). The WEB is a thermal isolating composite structure with cocuredthermal control surfaces and an ultralightweight hydrophobic solid silica aerogel whichminimizes conduction and radiation. This design provides excellent thermal insulation atlow gas pressures and meets the structural requirements for spacecraftlaunch loads andfor a 60 g impact landing at Mars without damage to the insulation or structure. (...)",https://www.jstor.org/stable/44725574). The use of these technologies or alternative onesneeds being assessed for L4 Enceladus Lander. The activity encompasses the followingtasks:Requirements consolidation and assessment of state of the art- Design of breadboard and associated test bench- Manufacture of breadboard, test bench- Execution of tests and exploitation of results- Conclusions elaboration and roadmap for further development towards a flight applicationThe outcomes of this activity are extendable to other planetary missions.
title: HIGH PERFORMANCE INSULATING MATERIALS FOR L4 ENCELADUS LANDER - EXPRO+

description: ESA operates one of the world's largest Earth Observation (EO) data archives, with data from missions dating back to the mid 1970s.Preserving these datatogether with the information and tools needed to interpret and use themis essential to analyse long-term environmental changes and support future decision-making. Within the EOF-EOS framework, long-term preservation of ESA's EO data holdings (Heritage Missions, Earth Explorers, Third Party Missions) and associated information and software is ensured through the Space Data Preservation System (SDPS), with assets located at ESRIN and external sites.Despite major progress, a significant volume of EO heritage data remains stored on legacy media at ESRIN and still requires transcription, recovery, and preservation in line with international standards. Beyond preservation and access, heritage data must be curated and improved to ensure continuity and comparability with newer missions. The generation of thematic collections and geographical datasets has further enhanced their usability and value.The Preservation Assets Operations and Maintenance (PAOM) Service will:Operate, maintain, and evolve Space Data Preservation System (SDPS) assets located at ESRIN;Manage the ESRIN EO Legacy Media Archive and Transcription Chains and perform legacy media transcription and data recovery;Generate thematic collections and geographical coverages using heritage data;Manage the ESRIN laboratory activities in support to transcription chains set-up and Philab Air Quality Platform activities, and manage and maintain the ESRIN AF Antenna;Support local visits at the Heritage Missions Walkthrough and Memorabilia Wall located at ESRIN and heritage missionsrelated outreach activities.
title: PRESERVATION ASSETS OPERATIONS AND MAINTENANCESERVICE (PAOM-SER)

description: Large optical antennas provide higher gain and sensitivity, ensure high data transmission rates,improve weak-light signal detection and are therefore necessary in photon starving regimesapplications as interplanetary, deep space and quantum communication. Segmenting the mainmirror is a very cost-effective solution when building large telescopes. However, large collectingareas of superior optical quality per se are not sufficient to achieve the alignment performancerequired to transmit entangled photons over long distances without decoherence. Co-phasingdifferent mirror segments with the accuracy required for quantum communication protocolsconstitutes an acknowledged challenge.This activity aims to develop, test, and validate a breadboard co-phasing system for segmentedmirror telescopes for single mode fiber coupling, supporting next-generation quantumcommunication networks, long-distance optical links, and turbulence-free telescope operations. Thesystem shall be suitable for the alignment of large (6 m and above) segmented mirror antenna andshall grant the wavefront distortions, focus, and tip-tilt continuous correction. The system shallactively adjust themirror positions to compensate for thermal, mechanical, gravitational flexure, andother environmental disturbance to enhance beam quality, coupling efficiency, reduce optical losses,maintain interferometric stability and improve single-photon detection efficiency to support satellitebased Quantum Key Distribution (QKD).Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors(incl. SMEs).  For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

description: Objective: To derive a standard set of requirements for the ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) Security Module and implement a prototype form-factor equivalent ADHA module.Description: The ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) has been initiated through a collaboration between ESA, European satellite primes and data handling equipment suppliers. The initiative has resulted in the agreement on an architecture for data handling unit based on standard module functions. A standard module procurement flow has been defined, as well as a standardized backplane connector and electrical interfaces. This allows independent development of interoperable modules that can be connected together in ADHA units. More advanced security functions are expected to be required in future ESA missions. The modular format of the proposed solution will enable faster adoption, and verification of new security technologies, in different unit configurations. This activity aims to perform analysis work to derive a standardization of the security function within an ADHA module form-factor, to allow the development of ADHA-compliant security products, which can be utilized together with other existing ADHA products, such as ADHA OBC. When implemented in the ADHA 3U form factor, such units are of particular interest for use in mid-size satellite platforms as well (less than 500kg mass). For prototyping purposes, the target of this activity is an elegant breadboard (EBB) of the ADHA security module in 6U format, based on the security function requirements defined in this activity. The extended format will provide the required design margins for the prototyping and demonstration phase. The long-term goal, this technology development, is the adaptation of this security module to an ADHA 3U module form factor. This activity encompasses thefollowing tasks: - Analyse the use-cases for dedicated security modules in data handling systems, both for platform and payload - Derive the detailed generic requirements for ADHA Security Modules, including functions, performances, electrical and software interfaces, etc. and present the specifications for review of the ADHA consortia and industrial working group - Derive the architectural design of a prototype ADHA Security Module - Derive a prototype electrical and software design of an ADHA Security Module, as an EBB in ADHA 6U format. - Perform functional validation of the prototype and demonstrate a representative use-case for the ADHA Security Module - Derive a roadmap for bringing the derived design to an ADHA 3U security module EM/EQM/FM.
title: ADHA SECURITY MODULE - EXPRO+

description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop and test a prototype terminal capable of DVB-S2X and RCS2 real-time switching in the return link utilising a Commercial-off-the-Shelf (COTS) modem ASIC. In a second step, the activity will develop a hub burst demodulator and scheduler, capable of using both, DVB-S2X and RCS2 frame types, allowing aflexible bandwidth share based on traffic types. End-to-end testing will include performance evaluation of the full return link comprising hub and user terminal.TargetedImprovements: Increase return link spectral efficiency up to 30% and demonstrate throughput beyond 100 Mbaud while retaining the intrinsic flexibility of MF-TDMA to retain low latency for lowthroughput applications.Description: In 2024 DVB updated the DVB-RCS2specification to include non-geostationary satellite systems. This allowed DVB-S2X constant or burst mode in the return link, allowing higher spectral efficiency and throughput. DVB-S2X and RCS2 can be mixed within the return link time plan, and a single terminalcan theoretically switch between them on the fly. This allows the increase of return link spectral efficiency up to 30%, through the implementation of S2X in the return link to carry traffic requiring large frames in a steady stream more efficiently, while retaining the ability to carry bursty, small packets more efficiently the majority of the time.This activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- In the first phase, the activity will focus to develop the software controlling the COTS modem ASIC and to develop aprototype terminal capable of DVB-S2X and RCS2 real-time switching in the return link and to test and evaluate the performance in alaboratory environment. The budget for this phase is up to 750 kEuro.- The second phase will develop a hub burst demodulator and scheduler, capable including a software or FPGA-based burst demodulator capable of switching between DVBRCS2- based MF-TDMA and DVB-S2X frames in real-time. A scheduler algorithm will be developed and tested able to accommodate the expected traffic types, with intelligent switching between frames as needed. Finally end-to-end testing will include performance evaluation of the full return link comprising hub and user terminal in a relevant environment.
title: FRAME-BY-FRAME SWITCHING OF DVB-S2X AND RCS2 IN RETURN LINK (ARTES AT 3C.053) (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)

description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, develop, launch and test autonomous and intelligent avionics enabling satcomconstellation satellites to operate autonomously across multiple environmental conditions in Low Earth Orbit (LEO). Breadboarding and in-orbit testing of critical platform functions including health monitoring, orbital control and resourcemanagement will be carried out. As part of the in-orbit experiment, a payload technology demonstrator will be developed to experiment with innovative approaches of autonomous payload configuration and control.Targeted Improvements: Enabling autonomous operation and reconfiguration of a satellite in a range of orbital LEO environments. This entails orbital control, platform resource management, health monitoring capability, autonomous decision-making capability and autonomous communication to ground.Description: Satellite operators currently face limitations when relying on single orbits (e.g. geostationary or low Earth orbit) for communications. These limitations affect system performance, resilience, and service continuity, especially in the aviation, maritime, governmental, and remote enterprise networks sectors. There is a growing need for an intelligent on-board control system that is capable to operate constellation satellites in multiple orbital LEO altitudes and environments. Such avionics systems must operate reliably across multiple orbital shells under varying environmental conditions, such as radiation, power constraints, and thermal fluctuations, particularly in very low earthorbits. Developing avionics that could autonomously detect the need for adaptation/changes of orbit and will enable:- autonomous multi-orbit operation- orbital transfer- repositioning of satellites in fleet and constellations.The activity will develop an intelligent avionics module enabling autonomous operation. An experimental satcom platform and payload will be developed and an in-orbit experiment will be carried out across a large range of space environmental conditions (e.g. eclipse period, radiation levels, thermal loads) in LEO.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach:Phase 1 (budget up to 2 MEuro) will design, develop and integrate an intelligent avionics module to full engineering model enabling autonomous satellite operations.  Phase 1 will develop and test:- autonomous operations logic that enables real-time system response to varying environmental conditions- adaptive AOCS and GNC functions to adapt to different orbits- health monitoring and diagnostic decision-making- autonomous TTC communication to ground.Phase 2 will develop the flight engineering model of the avionics module. A satcom experimental payload will be developed tosupport experimentation with intelligent, autonomous payload reconfiguration (e.g. transmit power, beam pointing, coverage change, temperature stabilisation, etc.) to maintain services during dynamic events such as orbital transfers and changes to operational space environmental and resilience response to sub-system failure. Avionics and payload will be integrated into a satellite. Phase 2 will launch and operate experiments in multiple LEO altitudes and environmental conditions.
title: IN-ORBIT EXPERIMENT OF INTELLIGENT AUTONOMOUS AVIONICS ENABLING MULTI-ENVIRONMENT SATCOM SATELLITE OPERATION IN LEO (ARTES AT 3E.033) (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)

description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and launch a dual satellite in-orbit testbed for sensing and communication for low-power devices with both transmit and receive user capability and inter-satellite link.Targeted Improvements: Enabling the development of protocols and operations concepts for the communication and geolocation from space with low-power terrestrial devices.Description: There is currently no European in-orbit capability to test and validate low-power communication directlybetween LEO satellites and standard ground devices. This limits the development of protocols, modulation schemes, and system architectures for emerging applications in low-power geolocation, environmental sensing, and ubiquitous IoT connectivity. This activity will develop a test bed that supports the exploration of disruptive use cases in low power direct communications between terrestrialdevices and LEO satellites. The testbed will comprise two satellites operating in tandem that can (at a minimum):- Establish a bi-directional low power (Tx/Rx) communications link between satellite and terrestrial devices- Provide Inter-satellite links (ISL) between the two, supporting cross-traffic, redundancy as well as geolocation of devices and interference sources- Test new protocols (e.g. SigFox, LoraWan, Bluetooth) and modulation schemes optimised for low-power signals.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1 with a budget of up to 3MEuro will design and develop a dual-satellite payload testbed able to directly communicate with terrestrial low-power devices. It will mature the key technologies and communication protocols from using simulation and laboratory testing to demonstrate feasibility and system readiness for in-orbit demonstration. Deliverables from Phase 1 are a summary report and full engineering model.- Phase 2 will build the flight equipment, launch, and operate the dual-satellite platform toexperiment with direct low-power, low frequency communications in orbit. The in-orbit experiment will test real-time user communications, validate geolocation concepts, evaluate inter-satellite link performance and collect performance data to inform future protocol standardisation and system architectures. Deliverables from Phase 2 are a summary report and 2 x flight engineering models.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses
title: DUAL SATELLITE IN-ORBIT TESTBED FOR SENSING AND COMMUNICATION FOR LOW-POWER DEVICES (ARTES AT 3E.034)

description: Objective: The objective of the in-orbit experiment is to conduct an experiment and develop the ability of a stack of small satellites to be deployed from a launch vehicle. The activity will design and build a launch vehicle adapter, satellite deployer and compatible test satellite/s which will be subjected to an on ground and in-orbit experiment test campaign examining the deployment dynamics from a launch vehicle in microgravity conditions and subsequent orbit behaviour of the launch vehicle upper stage and test satellites.Targeted Improvements: Enabling a European or Canadian source for small satellite deployers for stacked satellites within the launch vehicle fairing, allowing for 50% increase in utilisation of the launchvolume compared to the current state of art.Description: Current satellite deployment approaches which integrate satellites on a vertical satellite payload adapter structure within a launcher fairing underutilise the available volume, limiting the number of small satellites that can be launched per mission. Stacked satellite integration could increase volume and mass utilisation by up to 50% for a given launch increasingthe number of satellites deployed per mission, reducing mission capex and reducing time to deploy an operational constellation. However, there are no European solutions currently in use for deploying multiple small satellites in a stacked configuration. A Small Satellite Design Guideline (SSGL) has recently been developed that provides design guidelines forplatform developers which allow for the horizontal and vertical stacking of multiple satellites in medium and heavy lift launch vehicles. This concept has carried out critical technology derisking through on-ground tests and simulations.This activity will make use of the SSGL and the activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1, with a budget of up to 4 MEuro, will design and develop the Stack Deployment Mechanism and LV adapter, Test Satellites and validate their mechanical and deployment performance in ground-based environments and simulations preparing it forthe in-orbit experiment. Deliverables from Phase 1 are Study Report and Full Engineering Models of the deployer and test satellites.- Phase 2 will build the flight equipment, launch, and operate the satellites. The structural performance of the stack will be monitored through the launch phase. The deployment performance will be investigated through satellite GNSS and attitude data, as well asrelative position and poise estimation from sensors based on the launch vehicle adapter. Data generated in this phase help to increase the precision of mathematical models and digital twins used for solving satellite motion during deployment and orbital mechanicsverification required to refine the SSGL. Deliverables from Phase 1 are summary report and flight engineering models of the deployer and test satellites.
title: IN-ORBIT EXPERIMENT OF A DEPLOYER FOR STACKED SMALL SATCOM SATELLITES (ARTES AT 3E.035) (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)

description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design build and test a scalable High Aspect Ratio Satellite (HARS) platform encompassing the development of an integrated avionics architecture (including core functionality, minimal harnessing and modular interfaces). A second phase will extend the work and develop a scaled engineering model of a HARS platform with integrated thermal solution and with integrated avionics. The design shall be applicable to HARS from 1m to 4.6m, and able to be scaled up to 8m.Targeted Improvements: - Reduction in mass by 25%- Reduction in AIT time by 50%- Half the overall part count compared to the current state of art for SatCom satellite in the 500-2500kg range.Description: High aspect ratio satellites allow for the efficient and fast development and deployment of satellite communications constellations. High aspect ratio platforms also offer distinct advantages for satcomapplications including enhanced solar power generation and large surface areas for payload antennas. Nevertheless, this concept presents challenges inthermal management, accommodation of standard equipment, accommodation in launch vehicles, deployment into orbit.Additionally, the effective production of high aspect ratio satellites will require design for assembly methodologies not currentlyin use.To address these challenges this activity will design build and test a scalable High Aspect Ratio Satellite (HARS) platformencompassing the development of an integrated avionics architecture. The design shall be applicable to HARS platform from 1m to 4.6m, and able to be scaled up to 8m.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1, with a budget of up to 2 MEurowill develop the enabling technologies resulting in an integrated avionics design and test them as a scaled engineering model. Thefunctionality of the platform shall include:1. Core avionics functions (OBC, Thermal, ADCS/AOCS, GNSS, TTC, FDIR).2. Modular interfaces to allow integration will peripheral equipment (AOCS sensors and actuators, data storage, thermal equipment, ISL, propulsionunits, payload/payload controllers).Deliverables of Phase 1 include a Summary report and scaled engineering model of the core avionics.- Phase 2 will extend the work and develop a scaled engineering model of a platform with a primary structure that includes anintegrated thermal solution and integrated harness. A structural solution for the stacking of additional HARS within the launch vehiclewill be included. A compatible satellite dispenser/payload adapter for integration into the Launch Vehicle will also be developed. The combined avionics/satellite/dispenser will be tested in a representative environment capturing the equipment level loads, equipment and structure interactions.Deliverables of Phase 2 include a Summary report, scaled engineering models of a satellite platform and dispenser.
title: INTEGRATED AVIONICS AND PLATFORM DESIGN FOR A SCALABLE HIGH ASPECT RATIO SATCOM SATELLITES FOR CONSTELLATIONS (ARTES AT 4C.074)

description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and test innovative III-V solar cell s processes and associated disruptive photovoltaic assembly technologies aiming to reduce the complexity, manufacturing and assembly time to meet the high demand of telecommunication satellites constellations. III-V solar cells will be developed and tested using thedeveloped processes along with flexible Photovoltaic Assembly (PVA) mini modules.Targeted Improvements: - Enabling a European source of III-IV solar cells and PVAs for satcom constellations by - At least a factor of 2 reduction of the epitaxial growth time- Enabling substrate reuse in the fabrication - Enabling a standardised and flexible PVA mini module for mass production of solar arrays.Description: In the space telecommunications sector, the shift from GEO satellites to LEO constellations requires advanced solar technologies that offer a balance of high performance, scalable manufacturing and proven reliability across diverse LEO mission profiles. Within this evolving landscape,III-V multi-junction cells remain the benchmark in terms of efficiency and performance, but complexity, manufacturing and assembly time must be significantly improved to meet the growing demand for constellations. In order to achieve this goal,innovative processes must be developed to increase the production capacity. Development efforts should not focus solely on solar cell technology but must also extend to the photovoltaics assembly (PVA) level, enabling the realisation of standardised modular and scalable PVA solutions tailored to constellation needs.This activity will focus on III-V solar cells and their associated PVA technologies. It will study and develop solutions to two main primary factors currently limiting the scalability of III-V solar cells:- Reducing epitaxial growth time at least by a factor of 2 by increasing the growth rate of III-V materials while maintaining high opto-electronic properties. For doing so, new and disruptive epitaxial growth processes must be developed.- Enabling substrate reuse in the fabrication through the implementation of innovative Epitaxial Lift-Off (ELO) processes either chemical or mechanical based. The ELO process provides a dual benefit, as it supports the production of flexible, ultra-thin solar cells (e.g. 30um thick) and contributes to reduce the use of critical materials in the substrate (e.g. Germanium recycling). A combination of a mechanical and chemical lift-off approaches will be studied and developed to optimise the overall ELO process.The resulting developed III-V based solar cells will be manufactured and tested. They will serve as a critical building block for the development of a flexible PVA blanket. Interconnection and encapsulation technologies will be developed and tested. Finally, a standardised and flexible PVA mini-module, designed to function as a plug-and-playbuilding block for mass production of solar arrays, will be developed and testedProcurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: SCALABLE PHOTOVOLTAIC TECHNOLOGIES FOR TELECOMMUNICATION CONSTELLATIONS MASS PRODUCTION (ARTES AT 4F.183) - EXPRO+

description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop an architecture of a fully digital active transmit and a fully digital active receive antenna with a high number of radiating elements (i.e.4000) and capable to generate a significant number of beams (i.e. 1000) to support MEO satellite constellations. A transmit and a receive scaled engineering model will be designed and developed and experimentally tested to evaluate the performance.Targeted Improvements: Enabling development to achieve fully digital beamforming with an increase of about a factor of two of number of beams in comparison to current state of art in MEO.Description: The first generation of medium-earth-orbit (MEO) satellite systems have been using passive antennas employing reflectors to generate multiple beams. In the second generation of MEO satellites, active antennas started to be adopted in combination with digital beamforming. Recent developments in this field have seen active antennas that offer global coverage, low latency, maximum flexibility, multiple gigabits per second capacity, independent electronic repointing of the individual beams, reduced interference, and coexistencewith GEO satellites sharing the same frequencies. Active antennas enable also RF-power-allocation reconfigurability amongst the beams. Today, there is a need to develop the next-generation MEO satellites for commercial and governmental applications. The main expected improvements are associated to increasedcommunication data rate and flexibility, requiring larger antennas and an increased number ofbeams.This activity develops an architecture of a fully digital active antennas with a high number of radiating elements (i.e. 4000) and capable to generate a significant number of beams (i.e. 1000). Radiating elements, beamforming network, and the thermal design components shall be designed, optimised, manufactured and tested. For the active components, existing commercial-off-the-shelf products may be used, prioritising European products. The digital processor development is not part of this activity. However, interfaces and interconnects between the digital beam ports of the fully digital antenna and the payload processor shall be defined, quantified and implemented. Use cases for different types of MEO orbits shall be evaluated including inclined orbits and equatorial ones. The antenna design shall exploit power efficient solutions to deliver digital beamforming tasks reducingthe processing in the digital domain. Recent advances in area of reconfigurable beam forming networks and exploitation of symmetries when designing beaming networks will bestudied.The scaled engineering models shall include active and passive RF and digital building blocks of the antennaand beamforming network and shall be scalable to meet the performance requirements of the difference MEO use cases
title: FULLY DIGITAL ACTIVE TRANSMIT AND RECEIVE ANTENNAS FOR EMERGING MEDIUM EARTH ORBIT CONSTELLATIONS (ARTES AT 5B.256)

description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, build and test a highly integrated and efficient millimetre-wave phased array antenna using advanced packaging solution for multi-chip,multi-technology assembly, including 3-dimensional heterogeneous integration interconnects, thermal and power management.Targeted Improvements:Enabling disruptive technology to enable thermal management of highly integrated phased arrays, with a twice the RF power handling capability.Description: The development and deployment of millimetre-wave phased array antennas present several challenges that can reduce their efficiency and performance. These challenges include low RF power per element across different orbits (Low Earth Orbit (LEO), Medium Earth Orbit (MEO), and Geostationary EarthOrbit (GEO)) due to the use of silicon chips and the inefficiency in thermal management. Further limitations are introduced by the use of 2D packaging, which prevents the integration of high-power handling capabilities and enhanced thermal management technologies.The power efficiency and dependability of the antenna are reduced by signal strength degradation caused by the low RF output power per element. These performance issues directly affect satellite-to-ground communication as well as intersatellite communication.Toovercome these limitations, transitioning from 2D to 3D Heterogeneous Integration (3DHI) interconnect technology can significantly improve the thermal and power performance of phased array antennas. By stacking components vertically, more space can be allocated for effective thermal management, and the integration of multiple layers with thermal vias allows for better heat dissipation. This approach also enables the integration of diverse materials and technologies within the same package. Novel materials like Gallium Nitride (GaN) and Silicon Carbide (SiC) offer superior thermal conductivity and higher power handling capabilities compared to traditional silicon. Incorporating thesematerials into the antenna array, using an Integrated Antenna-on-Chip (AoC) approach, can increase the RF power per element while alleviating thermal constraints.This activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1 will develop an antenna concept, investigate and develop key processes necessary to fabricate a millimetre-wave 3DHI active antenna.This includes integrating low-power silicon chips, RF power amplifiers, thermal management solutions and advanced packaging techniques. During this phase, critical components will be developed to breadboard level to assess the effectiveness of 3D packaging methods, such as vertical integration and thermal vias, in addressing thermal dissipation and RF power handling challenges. Phase 1 outputwill deliver an antenna concept supported by critical breadboard test results. The budget for Phase 1 is up to 1,000 kEuro.- Phase2 will focus on developing a scaled engineering model of a millimetre-wave phased array antenna using 3DHI technology in Q, V, orW-Bands. Phase 2 will include refining the design, manufacturing, and testing the antenna's performance in representative operational environments.
title: HIGHLY-INTEGRATED AND EFFICIENT MILLIMETRE-WAVE PHASED ARRAY ANTENNA USING ADVANCED PACKAGING SOLUTION (ARTES AT 5B.258)

description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and test a Ka-band based (Ka-only or Ka and Ku) dual-beam electronically scanning flat panel antenna able to simultaneously connect to two satellites located at two different orbits. Four beams, two for transmit and two for receive path , will be implemented with two apertures.Targeted Improvements: - 50% antenna surface reduction required for the generation of 2 simultaneously active antenna beams compared to conventional phased array implementation.- Complexity reduction of the associated beamforming networks compared to phased arrays based on digital beamformers or multi-band beamformers.Description: The growing trend of combining the use of GEO and NGSO satellite systems for the provision of in-flight connectivity to airplanes suggests the use of antenna terminals able to connect simultaneously to two satellites located on different orbits. A possible operational scenario could envisage the use of LEO satellites for latency-sensitive content to be supplemented by GEO satellites connectivity, possibly over congested areas that are commonly found in lower latitudes that do not require extreme antenna scanning angles to connect to equatorial orbits. At higher latitudes, two concurrently operated antenna beams could simultaneously connect to two LEO satellites to provide aggregate data traffic. The approach of deploying a single antenna aperture per antenna beam leads to doubling the overall terminal surface occupation. Alternatively, producing more than one beam from a single array of radiating elements would require complex design for the radiating elements themselves as well as for the associated beam-forming network. The observation that connecting to NGSO systems does not require scanning the antenna beams to very wide angles suggests that the inter-element spacing can be relaxed, allowing for interleavingtwo simple arrays sharing a common antenna surface, each array could then be fed by a simple single-beam beam-forming network, resulting in a practical implementation.This activity will design a dual-beam electronically scanning flat panel antenna to exploit a common surface to implement two simultaneously operating antenna beams connecting to two satellite operating from different orbits and possibly at different frequencies (Ku- or Ka-band), this for the transmitting as well as for the receiving antenna functions. This will result in an antenna aperture generating two independent receiving beams and a second one generating two independent transmitting beams. A reduced scale prototype of a dualbeam flat panel antenna, either operating in transmit or in receive mode, will be developed and tested.
title: DUAL-BEAM KA-BAND-BASED MULTI-ORBIT AERONAUTICAL FLAT PANEL ANTENNA (ARTES AT 7C.106) - EXPRO+ (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)

description: The objective is to develop a standardised test laboratory to evaluate the coexistence of various satellite and terrestrial systemswithin a realistic, emulated, and controlled environment.TargetedImprovements: Enable a quantified and objective assessment of mutual interferences. Reduce satcom service outage due to interference from third systems to less than 0.1%.Description: Traditional methods of interference analysis and simulation, which often rely on static models and assumptions, are insufficient to describe thereal-time interactions and variability ofsatellite and terrestrial telecommunication networks. For example, in assessing the potential interference of new NGSO systems, it is mandatory to describe the dynamic radio resourceallocation strategy of the NGSO systemunder test to assess its dynamic effects on incumbent systems such as NGSO, GSO, or terrestrial mobile networks. Moreover, current analysistools are limited to assessing the interaction between the system under test and specific victim incumbent systems, ignoring the rest of the environment, i.e. additional incumbent systemsthat may also be affected. A standardised coexistence test laboratory is essential to address these challenges. By providing a controlled environment that accurately emulates real-worldoperational scenarios, this laboratory will enable a comprehensive evaluation of spectrum coexistence. The use of standardised plug-in modules, interfaces (e.g. API, RF, IF, DIFI), anddescriptors will facilitate the modelling of various satellite and terrestrial systems and their interactions, ensuring that the assessments are both accurate and confidential. The integrationwith external RF monitoring datasets will enable a digital synthesis of the RF spectrum to establish a background digital (and protected, i.e. sandbox) environment where the tests canbe performed.This activity will develop a test laboratory comprising hardware and software components following amodular and hierarchical approach, enabling future extensibility as well as follow-up/parallel developments. The activity will first establish a development framework, including development guidelines and requirements as well as interface specifications, and thendevelop key modules sufficient to provide an initial service.
title: SPECTRUM COEXISTENCE LABORATORY (ARTES 4.0 SPL 4S 3A.229) - EXPRO+

description: Objective: Objective of the activity is to develop and test positioning-independent techniques for Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) air interfaces.TargetedImprovements:Enable positioning independency for ground NTN terminals.Description: The development of a positioning-independent air-interface is deemed essential for future 6G NTN. Conventional 5G NTN terminals rely heavily on GNSS for positioning andtiming information, which means a terminal with no or poor GNSS reception cannot use NTN technology. Moreover, GNSS signals are vulnerable to spoofing and jamming,which can compromise the reliability and security of the communication links. By developing positioning-independent techniques, NTN terminals can operate without relying onGNSS or other positioning systems / sensors, enabling indoor coverage which is one of the goals in 6G for NTN as defined in the 3GPP roadmap. This feature is also crucialfor maintaining reliable communication in various scenarios, including critical infrastructure and emergency response. Positioning-independent modems can then operate inenvironments where positioning signals are weak or unavailable, such as indoors, urban canyons, or remote areas. This flexibility enhances the overall coverage and reliabilityof NTN services.This activity will explore the use of alternative techniques and protocols enabling a positioning-independent NTN air interface. Techniques and protocols shall be implementedin a modem prototype and evaluated in a real-time testbed possibly based on open radio stack.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs).  For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses
title: POSITIONING-INDEPENDENT AIR-INTERFACE TECHNIQUES FOR 6G NON-TERRESTRIAL NETWORKS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 7B.092) - EXPRO+

description: The objective(s) of this activity are the following:a) Design and implement an end-to-end Space Segment testbed that can constitute a security reference architecture, including a number of cyber security building blocks.b) Perform a security assessment and verification of the implemented security measures using the selected cyber security building blocks.c) Identify potential security enhancements, that can constitute candidates for further technical developments into products.The targeted current Technology ReadinessLevel (TRL) of this activity is 4 [RD1].WORK TO BE PERFORMED1 Work LogicThe work will be organised in two phases and the following tasks:Phase 1: Definition of cyber security building blocks and Space Segment testbedoTask 1: State-of-the-art survey of mission scenarios, security threats, relevant legislations and regulations and security technologiesoTask 2: Consolidationof Space Segment modular security reference architecture, including identification of required cyber security building blocks andspecification of system Space Segment security requirements.oTask 3: Specification of Space Segment testbed requirements (including incorporated cyber security building blocks), design and implementation and test planningPhase 2: Development, implementation and testing of cyber security building blocks and Space Segment testbedoTask 4: Development of the Space Segment testbedoTask 5: Space Segment Testbed Testing, Security Assessment and Vulnerability MitigationoTask 6: Lessons learnt and proposed roadmap for further (other than [RD16] building blocks development (including high level specifications)Note that phase 2 will be authorised to implement the agreed building blocks, subject to a successful Phase 1 and acceptance of a proposal for the conversion of the Phase 2 price from ceilingprice to Firm Fixed Price.
title: CYBER SECURITY BUILDING BLOCKS FOR SPACE SYSTEMS

description: Approved at CM25 under Component 3: Future PNT Demonstrators of the FutureNAV Programme, NovaMoon is a lunar-based local differential, selenodetic/geodetic and timing station that will enhance Moonlight and LunaNet lunar PNT services and support lunar scientificexperimentation.  This activity comprises Phases B/C/D/E/F of NovaMoon and is organized in three incremental builds, the development of which would allow to reach the full NovaMoon configuration (meeting all NovaMoon mission objectives) with NovaMoon Build3 aimed to fly on Argonaut2. NovaMoon Intermediate Builds1 and 2 will be designed to be as lander independent as possible (providing maximum flexibility in terms of lander opportunities). NovaMoon aims to demonstrate the following main objectives:1. Reference localPNT differential station (< 1 metre accuracy in real time),2. International Advanced "geodetic" Lunar Reference Station (< 10 cm accuracy),3. International "Lunar Time-reference" Laboratory ( ns-level).
title: NOVAMOON PHASES B/C/D/E/F

description: The activities will be performed in parallel with the Space Rider Programme Phase D.The scope of the procurement is to cover the activities related to the design, validation, installation, and operational support of a primary radar at the Landing Site in Santa Maria, Portugal.The system will be required to track Space Rider during the final part of its re-entry in order to verify that the descent trajectory is safe and nominal and, in case of anomalies, to support intervention actions aimed at neutralizing the spacecraft, thereby avoiding injuries to people and/or damage to property in the vicinity of the landing site.

title: COPERNICUS FLIGHT OPERATIONS SUPPORT SERVICE

description: This activity addresses the evolution of small satellite platforms toward sustainable space operations, in line with ESA's Zero Debris objectives and Ecodesign policy. It aims to consolidate system-level requirements for the next generation small satellite platform, integrating space debris mitigation constraints and environmental sustainability considerations across the full life cycle. Building on previous ESA and industry studies, the activity will identify key design drivers, perform trade-offs, and define a baseline platform concept up to System Requirements Review (SRR) level. It will also assess enabling technologies, engage with European suppliers, and establish a roadmap toward platform maturation and future demonstration. In parallel, the activity will analyse mission scenarios, hosted payload opportunities, and commercialisation aspects to support the preparation of a potential In-Orbit Demonstration (IOD). Overall, the objective is to support the development of reusable satellite product lines that embed Zero Debris compliance and Ecodesign principles while maintaining technical and economic viability.
title: S3-CL-15 ECOSTAR-S CONSOLIDATION PHASE - EXPRO+

description: There is an increasing trend towards collaboration among space agencies and a rapidly growingnumber of commercial space actors. This raises the scenario and challenge of how different partiescan cooperatively operate shared space assets through distributed access control mechanisms.The standard approach to manage access to a shared asset, e.g., hosted payloads, where one ofthe collaborating parties assumes full authority over the asset, while the other parties strictly rely onthis authority, may be too rigid for manyemerging use cases. Modern concepts such as launch rideshares, ground segments and platforms as a service models, or even token-based economiccommercialisation of space missions require a more fully collaborative approach.Thus, in the pursuit towards true collaboration and along trends such as web3 and Blockchain, thisactivity shall aim to demonstrate fully distributed identity and accessmanagement. DecentralisedLedger Technologies (DLT) shall be leveraged to support associated operations concepts andmanage credentials and policies for individual actors interacting with the space assets. DLTsolutions differ in key aspects regarding cybersecurity, performance and scalability thus a specificemphasis shall be placed on measuring overheads in terms of data, network traffic and computingpower in the constrained environment of space systems. DLT applications shall be identified andtested in support of:- managing credentials and access to collaborating space assets in a distributed manner- public key certificates including revocationand enforcement (e.g., revoke access of a specificoperator)- distributed identity establishment (e.g., how parties trust each othersendorsement of actors)- cryptographic key management and root of trust aspects (e.g., securely managing keys via trustedhardware and use of merkle-tree hashs and proof of inclusion concepts)
title: T709-801GD DLT-BASED ACCESS MANAGEMENT FOR THE (CO-)OPERATION OF SHARED SPACE ASSETS (EXPRO+)

description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop a European g-NodeB (gNB) hardware and software protocol stack architecture for regenerative NGSO satellite with a fully European signal processing platform, i.e., both hardware and softwareTargeted Improvements: Enabling a European full gNB in Space for regenerative 5G/6G broadband satellite systems not existing today in ESA Member StatesDescription: The 3GPP standardisation group has defined the necessary features and enhancements in 5G mobile broadband systems tosupport non-terrestrial network (NTN) since Release 17 in 2022. The upcoming 6G NTN integration into the terrestrial telecom systemenables new features such as:a. Seamless interoperability between terrestrial and satellite networks;b. Direct-to-device connectivity without specialised satellite terminals in FR 1 (i.e., <7GHz);c. Ubiquitous connectivity across geography;d. Broadband servicesfor aviation, maritime, and cross-border mobility;e. AI-Native networking to optimise beam management, manage mobility, and dynamically allocate spectrum across the multi-layered satellitenetwork.However, today no European solution exists for a full gNB signal processing hardware platform and software protocol stack as needed for 5G/6Gregenerative NTN payloads.This activity will develop a European gNB hardware and software protocol stack architecture for regenerative NGSO satellite with a fully European signalprocessing platform, i.e., both hardware and software. The gNB shall be able to support high throughput 5G/6G connectivity either in S-band spectrum(e.g., up to 50Mbit/s) or in Ka-band spectrum (e.g., up to 1Gbit/s).The activity will: Develop a concept of an efficient signal processing hardware and software protocol stack architecture for a European gNB implementation for regenerative NGSO satellites. Identify a suitable European signal processing platform and characterise relevant functional blocks of the signal processing hardware. A laboratory breadboard will be developed together with electrical ground support equipment (EGSE) suitable to performradiation characterisation including Single Event Effects (SEE), Displacement Damage (DD), and Total Ionizing Dose (TID). A radiation mitigation approach shall be developed and implemented using a combination of software- and hardware-based solutions to compensate for identified critical performance impacts. The devicewith the applied radiation mitigation measures will be radiation tested,and the performance will be compared to the unmitigated hardware performance. Carry out analysis and concept trade-offs to ensurethehigh throughput connectivity and minimised power consumption per MHz in the selected band (S-band or Ka-band)Identify and assess relevant in-orbit experiment considerations.
title: CONSOLIDATION OF A FULL G-NODEB FOR SPACE BASED ON A EUROPEAN SIGNAL PROCESSING PLATFORM (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.089) - EXPRO+

description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to enhance the existing Open Radio Access Network (ORAN) framework to support 5G/6G Non-Terrestrial-Network (NTN) payloads, while integrating the ORAN adaptations with conventional ground segment control centres.Targeted Improvements:1) Adapt the of Enhanced Open Radio Access Network (ORAN) interfaces to support Non-Terrestrial-Network (NTN) 5G/6G payload2) Improve the ORAN Transport network layer3) Enable the Integration of ORAN interfaces into the ground segment operations for system interoperability4) Enable new applications for NTN payloads.Description: Open Radio Access Network (ORAN) specifications are on the brink of reforming the 3GPP radio network fabric through the development and standardisation of open interfaces that provide vendor interoperability, disaggregation of radio protocol stack, access to Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML enabled Radio Intelligent Controllers (RICs) and a framework for Service Management and Orchestration (SMO). The complexity required for the management and optimisation of hybrid TN/NTN (terrestrial/non-terrestrial network) radio platforms, make ORAN an ideal candidate for handling mobility, resource allocation, quality of Service optimisation, multi-connectivity, and spectrum sharing amongothers.Currently a solid background exists to build upon and expand the current ORAN standards and interfaces to support the NTN regenerative payloads, the interworking between TN/NTN nodes and the open interface integration with ground segment Network Operations Centres (NOCs).To tackle the main challenges, this activity is expected to:1) Enhance ORAN architectures with respect to the deployment of optimised interfaces between ground and space.2) Support the adaptation of the ORAN application protocol and service models, to support the 5G/6G NTN payloads.3) Optimise the ORAN transport network association to support the satellite motion out of aspecific geographical area.4) Develop and test real and non-real time Radio Intelligent Controller (RIC) enabled AI/ML applications (xApps, rApps) for NTN node mobility, traffic steering, quality of serviceoptimisation and resource allocation.5) Integrate the ORAN open interfaces with a real or emulated/simulated NOC terminating the interface, to optimise the resource allocation of regenerative NTN nodes.6) Integrate the TN and NTN existing nodes under the same RIC and Service Management and Orchestration (SMO) platform.7) Deliver an end-to-end testbed that follows the OpenRAN workflow and demonstrate the performances for various scenarios with different service requirements.
title: OPEN RADIO ACCESS NETWORK FRAMEWORK FOR THE END-TO-END MANAGEMENT OF REGENERATIVE NON-TERRESTRIAL-NETWORK ACCESS NODES (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.039)

description: The aim of this activity is to establish a robust and validated greenhouse gas emissions baseline for the European space sector in support of ESA's broader decarbonisation roadmap. The work includes defining the sector scope and system boundaries, developing a harmonised accounting methodology, collecting and consolidating data from relevant stakeholders, quantifying emissions for a referenceyear, validating results, and preparing outputs that can directly inform future decarbonisation actions, target-setting, and strategic decision-making across the sector.
title: ESTABLISHMENT OF A GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSIONS BASELINE FOR THE EUROPEAN SPACE SECTOR - EXPRO+

description: NOSTRA is a multi-static radar architecture system to detect and track small debris in the few centimetres regime. The objective ofthis activity is the detailed design of the radar system architecture, of the signal and data processor and of the interfaces. The activity shall end with a Critical Design Review.
title: S3-SD-04: NOSTRA SYSTEM DESIGN - EXPRO+

description: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) safeguards system is designed to verify States' legal undertakings to use nuclear material for exclusively peaceful purposes. States declare their nuclear material and activities to the IAEA, and the IAEA verifies thecorrectness and completeness of these declarations.This requires robust and resilient GNSS trackers which can withstand sophisticated attacks (jamming, spoofing, and especially treacherous meaconing) and tampering attempts by State-level actors, providing Assured PNT (Trusted positioning data).The GNSS tracker shall be battery powered and capable of unsupervised operations. In previous projects (in particular, EL1-077) building blocks for this technology have been developed. The IAEA has expressed interest in a joint project to increase the protection against additional attacks identified and to raise the TRL level and to make the tracker ready forcommercialization. The objective of the activity is to study, design, implement and demonstrate a resilient and robust GNSS tracker to support IAEA safeguards activities, and other similar activities requiring Assured PNTThe tasks to be performed shall include:Based on EL1-077, the activity will study, design, implement and demonstrate the technologies required for the GNSS tracker, capable of detecting and mitigating jamming, meaconing and spoofing attacks, with focus on concrete uses cases and attack scenarios identified by IAEA.Additional technologies (for example tightly coupled INS and CRPAs) will be integrated into a functional prototype. As part of the demonstration, the prototype will be subject to thorough tests representative of challenging jamming, meaconing and spoofing scenarios mounted by capable attackers.The activity is part of a roadmap to make available to customers GNSS trackers with Assured PNT and will bring the technology to a TRL which will allow industry to make confident proposals for an Element 2. The activity will not include any Galileo PRS technology, as per NAVISP Declaration.
title: NAVISP-EL1-130-ROBUST GNSS TRACKER FOR SENSITIVE APPLICATIONS - EXPRO+

description: Development of a compact optical atomic clock module (physics package) for PNT applications. The activity will design, manufacture,and test an Engineering Model (EM) of a chip-scale optical clock exploiting an atomic optical transition to achieve 10 improved stability (target timing drift 10-30 ns/day) versus existing microwave clocks. The clock will provide a stabilized optical frequencyoutput in a low-power (< 5 W), compact device. Tasks include detailed thermo-mechanical design for robust operation in harsh environments, definition of low-power control electronics requirements and autonomous operation algorithms, assembly of the optical clock physics package, and development of Electrical Ground Support Equipment (EGSE) to control and test the EM. The EM will undergo performance verification in ambient and thermal conditions to demonstrate its stability, targeting TRL 4-5 and paving the way for future space-qualified ultra-stable timing solutions for navigation and timing systems.
title: NAVISP-EL1-131-CHIP SCALE OPTICAL ATOMIC CLOCK FOR PNT APPLICATIONS EXPRO+

description: Today, mission ground segment systems face increasingly sophisticated and fast-movingcyber threats that can evade static or rule-based detection tools and overwhelm traditionalrecovery procedures. As attacks grow more pervasive, dynamic and subtle, currentapproaches, such as rule-based or ticket driven responses struggle to react at the requiredspeed, resulting in prolonged attacker dwelltime and potential disruption of critical missionoperations, if an attack is detected at all.Real-time automated responses or self-healing' mechanisms, such as fall-back tosecure/minimum configurations, runtime policy/rule change, trusted state reconstitution, orrapid tear-down and re-deploy of compromised systems, can reduce the time required tocontain threats. The aim is to reduce attacker dwell time and maintain service continuityduring otherwise high impact incidents. This activity addresses that gap by developing anddemonstrating a proof-of-concept autonomous self-healing architecture tailored to thecritical mission operations ground segment. It will provide an adaptive resilience mechanismaddressing detection, isolation and recovery with an emphasis on service continuity. Moderntechnologies and techniques are to be explored including:- declarative infrastructure as code for cloud-agnostic redundancy and recovery automation- decoupled micro-service isolation and zero-trust architectures- secure root of trust and immutable system configuration restoration- failure prediction- adaptive response mechanisms leveraging machine learning.The proof-of-concept demonstrator will be integrated into a multi-mission, cloud nativeground segment scenario, leveraging existing (Cyber) Security Operations Centres((C)SOC) monitoring and diagnostic capabilities to ensure operational relevance. It willdemonstrate end to enddetection, isolation, and recovery in the context of missionmonitoring and control systems operating in the loop.
title: T709-903GA SELF-HEALING ARCHITECTURES FOR CYBER RESILIENT GROUND SEGMENT SYSTEMS (EXPRO+)

description: Space Weather Centre for Spain Initial Establishment and Core Capability Developments: Part 1This activity will constitute the initial establishment and operation of a Space Weather Centre for affected stakeholders along with underpinning tools, capabilities and procedures required in order to deliver tailored high quality services to end users. A colocation of the development and operations teams shall be foreseen with the aim to streamline the R2O process, support team building and to encouragedirect feedback to research, optimising the use of facilities in ESAC.Part 1 shall include: Systematic mapping of end users and establishment of key contact points with users and stakeholders Establishment of a proactive engagement strategy and actions with the identified end users to ensure full understanding of end user needs and operational requirements Development of necessary IT infrastructure, tools and service operation procedures in order to operate the space weather front desk, initially on an 8/5 basis, with on-call support during periods of elevated space weather activity. description: To build a mezzanine board to interface with a CAN bus on the units' backplane.Description:As part of the APA (Advanced Power Architecture) initiative, a standardised approach is being developed for internal communication between APA modules within an APA unit. This activity supports that effort by designing a compact, reusable TM/TC interface based on the CAN bus, known for itsreliabilityand simplicity.The mezzanine will serve as a common building block / solution for all APA modules, reducing integration effortandpromoting consistency across designs. By consolidating all required components into a small footprint, it simplifies system architecture, supports modularity and eases procurement, manufacturing and recurrence.This activity focuses on developing a compact mezzanine PCB that integrates five essential components required for CAN-based backplane communication (FPGA or microcontroller, ADC, voltage reference, CAN transceiver and XTAL/oscillator). The goal is to consolidate these elements into a small 30x30 mm footprint, supporting a range of external interfaces and operating on a 3.3V supply.This modular solution aims to simplify internal communication across systems where CAN is the preferred protocol, offering a reusable and scalable interface.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Consolidate the CAN protocol implementation.- Architecture definition (evaluating if FPGA-based or microcontroller-based).- Identify two suitable options for each one of the 5 required components, prioritising compact packaging and cost.- Design a 30mm x 30 mm PCB accommodating the 5 components and ensuring signal integrity andmanufacturability, ready to be assembled into an APA module and to interface with CAN bus and the APA module.- Implement the software or the VHDL code with the CAN protocol.- Prototyping and testing, assemble and validate the board to confirm functionality and performance.Deliverables: Breadboard,ReportNOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

description: EGV Pilot is an ESA pilot study aimed at structuring, mapping and assessing the geodetic foundations required to support future Earth Observation missions and Earth system science. The activity focuses on the role of geodetic observations and products as foundational enablers for Earth system monitoring, mission preparation, and the generation of long term geodetic data records. It builds on internationally coordinated developments on Essential Geodetic Variables (EGVs), in particular within GGOS and IAG, and translates these advances into an ESA-relevant framework aligned with the Earth Observation Science Strategy (EOSS), FutureEO missions, and other ESA programmatic elements. The study will establish clear traceability between geodetic requirements, products, observing systems and future EO missions. It will assess the readiness and maturity of geodetic observations and products, identify missing or degraded capabilities, and analyse how future ESA space and ground segment infrastructures could strengthen the geodetic foundations. Explicit consideration will be given to synergies with ESA missions such as GENESIS and NGGM/MAGIC, as well as to preparedness for integration into Digital Twin Earth.
title: EGV-PILOT: GEODETIC FOUNDATIONS FOR FUTURE EARTH OBSERVATION - EXPRO PLUS

description: The goal of the ROSE L Companion Satellite Instrument Concept Study is to investigate a variety of instrument concepts suitable forimplementing a bistatic companion satellite to ROSE L. This includes examining different instrument options and configurations thatcould enable a more compact SAR instrument design, even if this leads to reduced performance across certain Level 1 parameters.Thestudy aims to build an understanding of the multi-dimensional trade space between various SAR instrument concepts, their parametervariations, and the resulting impact on Level 1 performance. This analysis will support the tailoring of the instrument design to meet a specific set of Level 1 requirements while also informing the scientific community about how sensitive these performance parameters are to overall instrument complexity. Ultimately, the study will used as an input to define an optimal set of mission requirements and identifying a suitable instrument concept for a bistatic ROSE L companion satellite.

description: ESA intends to implement a Zero Debris policy by 2030 and has a long-term vision for a sustainable and safe space environment leveraging on the development of a space circular economy.Large Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites in particular present significant risks, both in terms of potential collisions and ground casualty hazards resulting from uncontrolled re-entry.  The ESA's Clean Space Office has been pioneering the study of ADR since 2012, starting with the e.Deorbit study, followed by the ClearSpace-1 and the CAT mission in more recent years, under the ADRIOS initiative part of the ESA Space Safety Program. In the past years there has been growing interest in ADR services targeting large LEO debris objects. This topic has recently been the focus of discussions and studies between ESA and external stakeholders, including EUMETSAT in the frame of a feasibility study (e.g. CDF) and the European Commission(EC) via its ISOS framework. This led to the implementation of industrial activities for a 6 month ERASE phase 0 mission and systemstudy which was kicked-off Q1 of 2026.The activity proposed here is to further mature the concept of the ERASE mission up to the Preliminary Requirement Review (PRR) milestone. The result of the activity and the maturation of the ERASE concept should be in linewith the outcomes of an ESA Preliminary Requirements Review as described by the ECSS. If successful, ESA intends to follow this study by the  Phase B1 and a eventual full mission implementation acceptance after CMin 2028

description: One of the main objectives of the Space strategy for Europe is to foster a globally competitive and innovative European space sector, in particular by improving support to technological maturation for sub-systems, equipment and technologies, including in-orbit demonstration and validation activities, to reduce time to market.To ensure the European Union non-dependence and competitiveness in technologies, there is a clear need for a regular, sustainable, cost-effective and responsive In Orbit Demonstration/Validation (IOD/IOV) service in the European Union. Space flight heritage in real conditions and environment is often required to de-risk innovations such as new technologies, products, concepts, architectures, and operations techniques are they for unique or recurrent, institutional or commercial missions.On 31 March 2023, the European Commission issued a Call for Expression of Interest for In Orbit Demonstration/Validation of Experiments Needing Aggregation, open until 15 March 2027 with multiple cut-off dates. The objective is to promote European competitiveness and non-dependence by offering flight opportunities through IOD/IOV for European Experiments. The European Commission pre-selects on a regular basis a number of Experiments that may fly with the Horizon Europe In-orbit Demonstration/Validation (IOD/IOV) Service.The SmallSat Project 2026 will provide the Horizon Europe In-orbit demonstration/Validation (IOD/IOV) service with a Carrier based on European SmallSat platforms, with a system total mass (including experiments) in the range of 250 kg.The SmallSat Project 2026 Contractor will be responsible for specifying and delivering all elements required to accommodate a set of experiments selected by the European Commission, in order to bring them into space and to allow for demonstration and/or validation purposes.These activities include:-system studies, at ground and space segments levels, including accommodation analysis of theIOD/IOV Experiments on the IOD/IOV Carrier and the compatibility analysis with the available launch solutions, -input to the launch mission analysis for the launch services provider, -manufacturing, assembly, integration and test of the whole IOD/IOV spacecraft based on EU manufactured solutions including the selected experiments, -ground segment capabilities (facilities and operators) to operate the IOD/IOV mission, -management of interfaces between the different IOD/IOV Experiments and the IOD/IOV Carrier, -inputs to launcher interfaces, -transport and delivery of the IOD/IOV spacecraft to the Launch Site, -launch campaign, -launch and Early Orbit Phase (LEOP), -operations of the IOD/IOV spacecraft for maximum one year taking into account the specific needs of the experiments, -delivery of the experiments in-flight data to the experiment providers, with a right to use for ESA and EU, -decommissioning of the IOD/IOV spacecraft at the end of the operations. This project is funded by the European Union. ESA is the Contracting Authority and runs the procurement under the ESA/REG/001 rev.5 adapted as per the signed FFPA Agreement.
