title: LUNAR NIGHT PCDU - EXPRO+

description: Objective: To develop a bi-directional DC/DC converter able to charge and discharge a generic storage system with a targeted reduction of 50% area and mass in the charge/discharge system.Description: Most of the current state of the art considers a dedicated converter for charging and a dedicated converter for discharging power into and from the energy storage system. This has impacts on the overall area and mass, as just half of the circuitry is in use at a given time. For those missions where mass and volume is a concern, a bi-directional converter allows to increase the power density and therefore to minimize mass and volume. In addition, currently the solution to charge and discharge an energy storage system is specific to the energy storage system in use. This activity aims to develop a bi-directional charge and discharge module, allowing the same circuitry to be used for charging and for discharging. The benefit of the bi-directionality reduces the area and the mass of the HW by 50%. On top, it is intended to analyze a generic solution to cover different energy storage systems (e.g. Li-Ion batteries and RFCS -Regenerative Fuel Cell Systems-). This provides a lot of flexibility, since the HW of the power management subsystem does not depend on the energy storage system, and therefore could be produced in advance. This also could lead to a reduction in time to delivery by 30%, by allowing recurrent use of the same design. The objective is challenging because the behavior of these storage systems is quite different and the converter must adapt to them. A charger/discharge module with bi-directional capability based on a non-isolated DC/DC topology with new switching devices (e.g.GaN based switches) and a versatile control system to adapt to the different storage systems. Possibly digital control may be considered to perform an adequate management of the battery or RFCS. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Confirmation of the scope of the charger/discharge (energy storage systems to be compatible with, power levels...) with a final consolidation of the preliminary requirements - Identify potential solutions (best topologies, control logic, switching devices...) and perform dedicated trade-offs to select a baseline - Design of the baseline, with the appropriate design analysis - Prototype manufacturing of a bi-directional charge and discharge module - Testing of a prototype - Analyse test results, identify and check deviations, implement corrections on the prototype if any to cover deviations to a final designDeliverables: Breadboard, Report
title: BI-DIRECTIONAL GENERIC CHARGE/DISCHARGE MODULE FOR GENERIC STORAGE SYSTEM - EXPRO+

description: SIMULUS is a framework for the development of space assets, developed by ESA, andavailable to ESA Member States under the ESA Software Community Licence. It is widelyused by European industry to develop spacecraft simulators, both in ESA contracts as wellas commercially. It is predominantly used for the development of operational simulators, thatsupport the training of operators for most ESA missions, but over the years, in particularsince it became available as ESA Software Community Licence, it has gained traction inother areas, e.g. onboard software validation facilities.With new players joining the sector (e.g. New Space) as well as increasing demand oncurrent industrial partners, a common feedback/request is to streamline the 15+ year olddevelopment process currentlyin place, as it is based on outdated/heavy/rigid developmentprocesses (e.g. Waterfall) while the sector is moving toward to more flexible/agiledevelopment approach, as it adapts to a wider family of missions, from cubesats to thetraditional ESA satellites.In today's space context, to support European industry to be more competitive, a simpler,more modern process is required, that not onlyreduce costs but also enables the scaling ofdevelopment of more simulators by industry. In such context, the proposed activity aims tosimplify the development process and the tools that support it, by revisiting the currentapproach in close collaboration withindustry. It is expected to reduce the number of manualsteps required to setup the simulator, the number of tools involved and reducing thedependency on costly 3rd party software.
title: T709-904GA TOWARDS A STREAMLINED DEVELOPMENT APPROACH IN SIMULATORS (EXPRO+)

description: Objective: To develop a complete Software product portfolio of building blocks facilitating the integration of ADHA platforms in Mid-size LEO satellite platforms.Description: The Advanced Data Handling Architecture (ADHA) has been developed as a set of hardware components with standardized communication interfaces. Previous work has focused on the hardware aspects, but the current situation highlights the need for a robust software stack to support ADHA in space missions, in particular mid-sized LEO satellites. The main concern is to ensure that enough software components are ready for use in flight and developed using modern, modular techniques to enhance compatibility and performance. This activity aims to provide a modular software stack that can be utilized across different ADHA-based computers, including On-Board Computers (OBCs) and Instrument Control Units (ICUs) from various vendors. By leveraging different European processors, FPGA, and other COTS processors commonly used in commercial satellites, the software stack is aimed at offering flexibility and interoperability. The added value includes improved mission reliability, reduced development time, and cost savings through standardized software components. The configuration and deployment of the software will be integrated into a model-based software development and code generation tools such as TASTE using Space Creator, facilitating streamlined development and deployment processes. Future activities may involve further refinement of the software stack, extending compatibility to additional processors, and continuous improvement based on user feedback and mission requirements. This activity encompasses the following tasks: -Assessing the feasibility of a modular software stack for different ADHA-based computers. - Developing the software stack to support multiple European processors. - Integrating the software stack into a software MBSE toolset (e.g. TASTE). - Testing and validatingthe software stack across different hardware configurations. - Documenting the development process and results. Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community Licence, allowing access and updates by individuals or entities within ESA Member States.
title: ADHA SOFTWARE ARCHITECTURE - EXPRO+

description: Objective: To design and assess the life cycle of an optimised harness including cables, connectors, and back-shell components, allmanufactured using eco-friendly processes and alternative materials.Description: Spacecraft harnesses are essential for power distribution, data transmission, and signal integrity within satellites and other spacecraft systems. However, conventional harness designs rely on materials and manufacturing techniques that have a significant environmental impact, such as PTFE (Polytetrafluoroethylene)-based insulation, gold and nickel plating, and energy-intensive production processes. The ecodesign harness initiative focuses on the development of a sustainable harness architecture, incorporating alternative materials and environmentally optimised production methods. This includes innovative approaches to conductors, insulation, jacket, connectors, accessories, tie bases, assembly processes and integration, all tailored for space qualification. This activity aims to minimise environmental impact while maintaining space-grade reliability and performance, contributing to the broader vision of sustainable space through responsible material selection, reduced emissions, and improved end-of-life strategies. A comprehensive life cycle assessment (LCA) will be performed to comparethe environmental impacts of the optimised harness against conventional designs, from raw material extraction through to end-of-life,including phases such as manufacturing, integration, launch, and decommissioning. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Trade-off analysis and environmental impact assessment. - Key environmental contributors identification. - Optimisation actions and technical feasibility. - Characterisation and LCA validation.Deliverables: Breadboard, ReportProcurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: ECODESIGN HARNESS FOR SPACE APPLICATIONS -EXPRO+

description: Objective:the proposed activity will provide the concepts of operations, system and programmatic assessments, and will specifically include:Mission (CONOPS) and requirements definition: redefine in detail the assumptions, the purpose and the general concept of operations (incl. storage, transport, attachment and disposal) objectives deriving consistently the system and interface requirements.Conceptual design: based on the mission definition and system requirements, a conceptual design of the RemoveApp system will be developed. This includes the basic layout of the system, the mass and size, the necessary subsystems (e.g. AOCS and propulsion)and the interfaces (e.g. mechanical, power) considering the compatibility with storage, servicer and target elements. description: Objective: The objective is to develop and validate an AI-powered autonomous satellite system capable of real-time threat detectionand mitigation targeting LEO constellations. This will reducereliance on ground-based monitoring and improve resilience in satellite operations.TargetedImprovements: - 50% improvement in real-time threat detection latency / delay over ground-based solutions.-60% reduction in response time using AI-initiated autonomous countermeasures.- Development of a simulator for cyber, RF and physical attacks, enabling validation of AI-based countermeasure/mitigation solutionsintroducing a novel capability in ESA MS.Description: Current satellite security solutions depend on ground-based infrastructure for threat detection and mitigation, introducing latency and operational risks. Traditional security mechanismsare static, rely on predefined protocols, and lack adaptability, making them ineffective against sophisticated, evolving threat scenarios.This activity will develop an AI-powered Autonomous Satellite Systemfor real-time cyber threat detection and mitigation. By leveraging AI-driven intrusion detection and automatedresponse mechanisms,the system will enable LEO satellites to autonomously identify, analyse, and counter cyber threats without reliance on ground intervention.Edge computing will facilitate real-time adaptive security policies, ensuring rapid response to attacks while significantlyimproving system resilience.To evaluate the concept, the activity will develop a reference cybersecurity architecture, incorporating an AI-powered intrusion detection engine, automated countermeasure execution,and simulation frameworks for cyberattack modellingand mitigation testing. The system will be deployed and validated using a FlatSat testbed, an attack simulator to model, test, andrefine simulated cyber-attack scenarios, and a simulator for the Inter-satellite link to validate real-time threat mitigation in context of satellite constellation. The simulator environmentshall be capable to analyse and validate AI-driven mitigation strategies across multiple simulated orbital assets in a constellation. Furthermore, the attack simulator model shall analyseand benchmark threat mitigation techniques for additional RF and/or physical threat scenarios.The expected outputs include a functional FlatSat testbed, an AI-driven intrusion detection engine for autonomous response to cyber and signal interference threats, and a simulationenvironment to model, test, and refine specific attack scenarios.
title: AI-POWERED AUTONOMOUS SATELLITES FOR THREAT DETECTION AND MITIGATION (ARTES 4.0 SPL 4S 3D.038) - EXPRO+

description: Objective: The objective is to design, develop and test an Automatic Identification System (AIS) spoofing detection system onboard the satellite for satellite-based maritime surveillance, offeringreliable AIS information with low-latency.TargetedImprovements: Reduce by half the latency of detection of non-reliable reporting vessels compared to current technologies. Decrease reliance on ground-based infrastructures by enabling onboarddetection of deceptive AIS signals.Description: With approximately 90% of international trade travelling by sea, maritime routes are becoming increasingly congested. A reliable maritime domain awareness is thus paramount toaddress critical security (e.g. submarine cables, piracy), safety (e.g. collision avoidance), economic (e.g. fleet monitoring) or environmental (e.g. illegal fishing) needs, and space-basedcomponents are critical due to the limited terrestrial systems coverage. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) is one of the main components of the current maritime domain awarenessinfrastructure, being mandated by International Maritime Organisation and enabling the reporting of vessels worldwide. However, the current AIS setup suffers from reliability issues.Vessels can arbitrarily either switch off their AIS transponder or use (or being the target of) malicious deceiving techniques such as AIS spoofing and jamming or manipulation of GNSSinformation embedded in such messages. This results in fictitious abnormal behaviours that are becoming increasingly common and causing significant disruption across entire regions.Moreover, traditional satellite-based AIS processing systems rely heavily on ground-based validation, leading to high latency in spoofing detection and reducing the effectiveness of real timecountermeasures.An onboard detection module could overcome these challenges by detecting in near real-time any AIS anomaly and initiate the mitigation countermeasures, i.e. paired with communicationto other trailing satellites or direct-to-device communication links (out of the scope of this activity), such detection system could inform users about fraudulent activities faster thantraditional surveillance systems.This activity will develop and test an onboard Automatic Identification System (AIS) spoofing detection system for satellite-based maritime surveillance, offering reliableAIS informationwith low-latency. Low latency AI-based anomaly detection and other technologies such as signal fingerprinting and deterministic algorithms will be investigated and developed.The AIS spoofing detection module shall be designed according to selecteduse cases and implemented on a software-defined radio-based payload and tested in a representativemaritime surveillance scenario to evaluate its effectiveness in detecting, localising, and mitigating AIS spoofing in real time.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture, and test a processor breadboard and associated software implementing a distributed unit (DU) onboard a satellite. TheDU will implement Radio Link Control (RLC) and Medium Access Control (MAC) functions, optimized for Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN), to address processing, memory andpower constraints, as well as service needs in terms of cells and user numbers The feasibility and implementation of control unit (CU) functions on the 5G g-NodeB (gNB)should be addressed by the activity depending on the selected 5G system split and targeted system capacityTargetedImprovements: - Increase the DU throughput by a factor of 10 with respect to currently existing terrestrial network solutions (TN) implemented on space representative hardware.- Increase by a factor of 10 the number of cells handled by the DU, with respect to existing TN solutions.Description: Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTNs) require optimized handling of link-layer functions to mitigate the effects of long propagation delays, fluctuating signal conditions, and limitedbandwidth. Conventional NTNs rely on extensive ground infrastructure to manage link-layer functions such as scheduling, retransmission control, and resource allocation.Implementing full CU/DU on-board with high throughput is currently unfeasible due to the high system bandwidth to route and the limited processing power available.This activity shall develop a high-throughput (target 100 Gbps) satellite router breadboard, integrating an onboard CU/DU implemented on a radiation-tolerant multi-coreprocessor.This activity will design, manufacture, and test a processor breadboard and associated software implementing a distributed unit (DU) onboard a satellite.The Radio Link Control (RLC) layer will provide:1. Segmentation and reassembly optimized for dynamic satellite link conditions.2. Retransmission control managed onboard to reduce latency and dependency on ground stations.The Medium Access Control (MAC) layer will handle:1. Onboard scheduling and resource allocation to optimize time-frequency resource use.2. Adaptive HARQ (Hybrid Automatic Repeat Request) to balance error correction and latency.3. Inter-beam coordination to optimize multi-beam traffic distribution. The CU shall perform real-time processing, ensuring efficient and reliable network operation withoutexcessive feeder link traffic. Engineering tasks include system architecture definition, hardware / software integration, and performance validation through breadboardtesting in a representative NTN environment.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and test a 5G NTN dual active modem prototype with active resource management for improving link reliability and performance, whileoptimizing the space segment resources utilization.TargetedImprovements:-doubling the peak data rate compared to state of art modems.- reduction by half link outage time.Description: The need for a dual-active modem in 5G Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) arises from the growing demand for reliable, high-performance communication links particularly inscenarios where terrestrial networks are unavailable or unreliable. A dual-active NTN modem can maintain two simultaneous satellite links, significantly reducing the risk ofoutages caused by shadowing, fading or interference. At the same time, it provides an additional communication channel that enables load balancing across space segmentnodes, helping to distribute traffic efficiently and improve peak user data rates. Active resource management is essential in this context. Strategies must be designed todynamically allocate resources based on real-time link conditions and performance metrics. These strategies should ensure that the satellite system can optimize keyperformance indicators, such as peak data rate and service availability, while minimizing the resources allocated to each link and network node (e.g. payloads). Developingcontrol plane methodologies is also a critical aspect of this solution. The control plane manages the signalling and control information required for the operation of thecommunication links. It enables the system to gather real-time measurements of links conditions, which are essential for making informed decisions about resource allocationand link management. These methodologies also provide mechanisms for communicating decisions to the network including satellites and user terminals ensuring that thesystem can adapt to changing conditions and maintain optimal performance.This activity will develop a prototype dual-active 5G modem, potentially based on open radio stacks, and implement a testbed to evaluate the prototype under realisticconditions. This testbed will include a channel emulator with multiple RF interfaces to emulate themultiple links. Channel performance as well as satellite system resourcesallocation will be tested for various operational scenarios, and both resource management methodologies and control plane techniques will be assessed.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and test a thin optical aperture leveraging advances in integrated photonic technology to reduce the size andweight of space-based optical communication terminals.TargetedImprovements:Reduction of both size and weight of satellite laser communication terminals by 50%.Description: Optical communication terminal solutions with lower size and weight are required to serve the increasing role of small spacecraft for satellitecommercialisation by maximising the amountof payload space for mission-enabling processing or sensors. State-of-the-art optical communicationterminals are often too bulky and heavy for such small platforms and a leap in technology is required. This activity will seek innovative integrated photonicsolutions to replace the telescope subsystem of an optical communication terminal and eliminate as much as possible the need for free-space propagationinside the laser terminal. By doing so, it is expected to greatly reduce the size and inertial mass of the telescope subsystem, enabling for instance furtherreductions in steering assembly size, weight and power.This activity will design and prototype a photonic aperture (or flat telescope) that shall provide good beam quality (for coupling/emitting into/from singlemode waveguides such as single-mode fibres), shall be relatively large (at least several cm in diameter) or provide enough optical gain to enable convincingreplacement of conventional beam expansion and free-space propagation optics (traditional telescope assemblies) in space optical communicationterminals. A foundry-compatible fabrication process of the photonic aperture shall also provide a low-cost telescope alternative by eliminating the need forexpensive optics and assembly and alignment touch labour.The following tasks are envisioned:- Identify the potential solutions and latest innovations in integrated photonic able to replace conventional optical aperture assemblies in space-basedoptical communications for small platforms and/or use cases where accommodation of optical communication terminals is drastically constrained bytheir size and weight.- Develop a preliminary design and expected performance of the chosen solution.- Manufacture and test a prototype and evaluate the performance in a representative laboratory environment.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and test a digital coherent and incoherent signal combining receiver that utilises multiple smalltelescopes, achieving a large effective collection area.TargetedImprovements:Reduction of system cost and complexity by using multiple small apertures to avoid the use of a larger aperture with an adaptive optics system whilemaintaining the total corresponding coupled power-in-fibre.Enabling modular system design, allowing incremental future upgrades to enhance link power budget.Description: The logical progression in optical receiver development is to use a modular receiver design with multiple apertures combined coherently and incoherently.Firstly, small aperture telescopes are significantly less affected by atmospheric disturbances and can operate with cost-effective hardware, such as tilt tracking.Secondly, advancements in large Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) and digital signal processing (DSP) blocks can significantly simplifythe optical part of the receiver and enhanced reliability, while shifting the complexity to the digital domain. Functional verification of proposed idea hasbeendemonstrated in laboratory environment by research groups.The present activity shall analyse and demonstrate via a free-space-optical experiment at minimum 10 Gbps for coherent and up to 10 Gbps for incoherentmodulation (e.g. DP-QPSK, OOK) receiver system over atmospheric turbulence conditions that are representative (or worse) of those encountered inGEO/MEO/LEO. A receiver should perform optical front-end conditioning, followed by digital coherent and incoherent multi-channel combination, and thenprovide an output toa modem.This demonstrator will feature, but not be limited to, the following critical functions: cost-efficient tilt-tracking stage, optical multi-channel front end unit withdigital coherent and incoherent combiner, electrical output to a modem.

description: Objective:The objective of this study is to develop a system concept evolving HydRON services to maritime communications and identify the technology gaps as well as the required development roadmap.Targeted Improvements:To enable maritime communications with satellite HydRON (High-throughput Optical Network) systemDescription:Maritime routes are strategic in a connected world, where economies are interdependent. 80% of the global trade depends on shipping. Current strategical routes include South China, South India, Suez Canal, Mediterranean see, trans-Atlantic and Panama Canal. Together with the current routes, the transit along the arctic seais currently becoming more attention for cargo ships but also for defence purposes. Climate change may enable the use of this route,which could mean a drastic reduction in transport costs and service time (reduction of 25-40% in distance). From a logistics perspective, cargo companies aim to monitor their goods and containers, while ports seek to receive advance information about incoming cargo to optimize and plan the unloading process.Additional to the commercial and logistic interests, the defence aspects connected to maritime communications are of special interest, especially in an arctic route, where any developed infrastructure, could enhanceresilience.Currently, maritime communications relay on low-data rate satellite communications, or the use of low-band frequencies, when the ships are located close to shore. HydRON provides space-space and space-ground connectivity, extending terrestrial networksin space and providing global coverage.The activity shall investigate user needs, requirements and system concepts for maritimecommunications (space-sea, sea-sea, sea-shore/ports), to extend the use of HydRON in maritime scenarios. Technology gaps and related technology roadmaps shall be developed, considering optical terminals and any critical technologies. The system shall consider themanagement of cloud-blockage by combining space communications with e.g. a maritime ship-to-ship free-space network or hybrid communications with RF. The space segment shall consider the coverage along the most used routes. The concept shall consider the combination of security sensitive communications with logistic traffic. Finally, the activity shall propose a demonstrator where the relevant technology as well as the operational concept can be demonstrated. The activity will also contribute to the evolution of ESTOL.
title: HYDRON MARITIME: SATELLITE OPTICAL NETWORK EXTENSION (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.239) EXPRO+

description: Objective:The objective of this study is to assess the feasibility of applying Common Criteria framework (or equivalent) to guarantee compatible security mechanisms with HydRON (High-throughput Optical Network).Targeted Improvements:To achieve security interoperability of HydRON with other networks with a clear protection profile definition in line with international standards.Description:Multiple constellations are expected to be developed in the coming years, addressing different applications, like navigation, Earth Observation and communications as well as defence. Each constellation will be optimized for the target application, in terms of technologies, coverage, but also security functions. The challenge, but also the opportunity is to make use of all the possible infrastructure to enhance coverage and resilience of these systems by the integration of optical communication security features like Low Probability to be detected or interfered (LPD/LPI).However, different users will have different protection profiles and thereforesecurity targets will differ between networks. The Common Criteria for Information Technology Security Evaluation (referred to as Common Criteria) is an international standard (ISO/IEC 15408) used to specify security functional and assurance requirements, to guarantee implementation and verification of the security features and it can be used as a baseline for the security analysis of different networks and interoperability of security levels.This activity shall define a set of protection profiles for different target users and identify the security targets for different networks. Taking HydRON as a baseline for communications, the activity shall consider additional, selected national or EC networks interconnected by optical links in space or with optical ground stations and ground networks.For such security interoperability, the activity will define the required security functions (confidentiality, integrity, availability, authentication, non-repudiation...) and achievable levels of assurance by the different space networks. For the sected networks, an analysis of the impact shall be performed for each of these security functions, including a preliminary assessment of vulnerabilities by different potential threat actors and its impact on the system. The feasibility of applying Common Criterialframework or similar framework for these networks shall be assessed. Additionally, the achievable level of protection by the different networks shall be provided as a draft catalogue, to be presented to potential users. The activity shall define initial access scenarios for Ministries of Defence (MODs) and Civil Security Entities to utilise the upcoming HydRON installation to conduct dedicated, potentially classified testingvalidating defencegrade security, resilience behaviours, and interoperability in realistic operational scenarios and providing inputs to preliminary vulnerability assessment analysing operational impacts of potential attacks.
title: HYDRON RESILIENCE: SECURITY ASPECTS OF NETWORKS INTEROPERABILITY (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.240) EXPRO+

description: Objective:The objective of this study is to investigate the High-throughput Optical Network evolution (HydRON EVO) as the backbonenetwork enabling a total capacity of tens to hundreds TbpsTargeted Improvements:To assess the feasibility of optical space backbone network with total capacity in the range of tens to hundreds TbpsDescription:Following the terrestrial network analogy, backbone (long-haul) networks provide capacity beyond Terabit-per-second (Tbps) per single line (with links beyond 800 Gbps per wavelength). The current HydRON (High-throughput Optical Network) demonstration system will demonstrate single-link communications from 2.5G to 100Gbps, addressing both user access and the lower datarate backbone links. To enable growth of optical space networks, as an extension of the terrestrial fibre network, a space backbone is required to support multi-Tbps capacity in space. The backbone should be interoperable and interface with multiple networks like the one developed in HydRON demonstration system. However, using DWDM technologies and commercial coherent transceivers, the single link capacity can be increased beyond Tbps, and by aggregating multiple channels the network capacity can be increased to tens or even hundreds Tbps.This activity shall address the design and technology trade-offs of a space network backbone exceeding several Tbps and serving other space networks. It shall provide a set of requirements and a system concept. It shall be verified by analysis that the system concept is scalable at higher rates. Interoperability aspects shall be analysed, to guarantee the connectivity among networks (including terrestrial fibre networks). Technology gaps shall be identified and technology roadmap provided. Finally, the activity shall propose a demonstrator concept where the relevant technologyas well as the operational concept can be demonstrated, to further push the technology borders in terms of data rates/capacity aiming to maintain the strategic leadership position of the Europen/Canadian Industry The activity will also contribute to the evolutionof ESTOL.
title: HYDRON EVO: MULTI TBPS SPACE BACKBONE NETWORK (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.241) EXPRO+

description: Objective:The objective of this study is to develop a system concept extending High-throughput Optical Network (HydRON) services to High-Altitude Pseudo-Satellites (HAPS) and their networks. To identify the technology gaps as well as the required development roadmap including estimations of schedule and costs.Targeted Improvements:To enable the connectivity of HAPS to an evolution of the satellite optical network system.Description:High-Altitude Pseudo-Satellites (HAPS) will play the role of an intermediate, airborne layer in a multi-domain/orbit communications architecture in line with the optical-6G concept. HAPS operate in the stratosphere at altitudes of 15 to 50 km, where they can maintain a near-stationary position for weeks or even months at a time. A single HAPS cancreate a wide-area communication cell that provides reliable connectivity to remote or rural areas where building traditional terrestrial infrastructure is uneconomical. A satellite-to-HAPS optical link can serve as a high-bandwidth feeder link, backhauling data from the HAPS to the satellite network and then to the terrestrial network, avoiding the need for a ground gateway in an inaccessiblelocation. HAPS can conduct long-term surveillance or monitoring missions over a specific area of interest, providing a significantadvantage over LEO satellites which only pass over a given point for a few minutes at a time. With an optical link, a HAPS can uplinkreal-time, high-resolution imagery and sensor data to a satellite (or another HAPS), enabling rapid analysis for applications like border security, environmental monitoring, or situational awareness. In the event of a natural disaster that destroys ground-basedcommunication networks, HAPS can be rapidly deployed to provide a temporary but persistent communications hub. The optical link to an optical backbone network like HydRON ensures that the HAPS remains connected to the global network, providing critical communicationcapabilities for first responders and civilians.The activity shall investigate user needs, requirements, and system concepts for HAPS-space bidirectional optical communications, to upgrade the HydRON System with an airborne layer. Technology gaps and relatedtechnology roadmaps shall be identified and addressed for any critical technology, including optical terminals. The system shall consider the management of cloud-blockage by combining space communications with e.g. a HAPS-to-HAPS free-space network or hybrid communications in RF. The concept shall consider the combination of security sensitive communications with logistic traffic. Finally, the activity shall propose a demonstrator concept where the relevant technology as well as the operational concept can be verified. The activity will also contribute to the evolution of ESTOL.
title: HYDRON HAPS: HAPS-BASED OPTICAL NETWORK EXTENSION (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.242) EXPRO+

description: Objective:To develop a portable modem that can be easily integrated in an existing optical ground station to make it compatible with ESTOL specificationsTargeted Improvements:Increased interoperability between existing optical ground stations and future satellite systems (e.g., HydRON).Description:There are a number of existing or planned optical ground stations (OGSs) that are currently used for scientific missions or to demonstrate quantum technologies. Those OGSs are not compliant to the ESA Specifications for Terabit/s Optical Links (ESTOL). To maximise the benefit of early Member State investments, the activity shall develop an upgrade kit" for multiple existing OGS infrastructures. An easy-to-integrate modem will facilitate the upgrade of such existing or planned OGSsand increase their interoperability with future commercial and institutional systems that will adopt ESTOL and its evolutions.Thisactivity shall develop a portable breadboard for an ESTOL-compliant modem. In the scope of the activity, it shall be assumed that thetarget existing OGSs have already been developed in terms of optical elements (e.g., aperture, adaptive optics, etc.) in order tobecompatible with ESTOL. The portable modem shall be connected to the optical part of the OGS by optical fibre, and it shall implement both transmit and receive functionalities. The modem breadboard shall come with a GUI and an interface control document to facilitate its fast and easy integration and use. The functionalities of the portable modem shall be validated in the Contractor's laboratory and in an existing selected OGS.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). description: ObjectivesTo increase the efficiency of photobioreactors by an improved design of light conduction anddiffusion inside the reactor.DescriptionThe need for regenerative life support systems for long term space missions necessitates a questfor increased efficiency of Photobioreactors. The light intensification of photobioreactors is animportant building block to increase the return on investment with respect to light energy introducedvs oxygen yield in a defined volume.Previous activities have identified as a priority the need to progress on specific technologies, suchas the type of light sources and on innovative materials for light conductionand diffusion (e.g.polymers, leaking rods, specific optical fibers, lightning fabrics). This activity attempts to push theboundaries of photobioractor efficiency even further (compared to BIORAT-1) by investigating amore efficient light diffusion and as well characterization of the impact on the process and thebiomass.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review the state of the art for light intensified photobioreactiors and energy efficient lightguidance systems- Design a test bench with realistic operational parameters (light, flow, active species etc.)and test the most optimal configuration to achieve best possible efficiency w.r.t. volumetricoxygen and biomass production- Assess the potential biological effects of immersed light sources and possiblecountermeasures against fouling and clogging- Provide a development plan for operational hardware on ground and in space includingMAIT aspects for an operational scenario and define the scaling laws.

description: Objective: To develop a representative demonstrator of a Scatterometer instrument based on a phased array with a reduced number of control points, by exploiting grating lobes.Description: For Earth Observation applications there are instruments, like Scatterometers, requiring a limited number of beams M pointing in fixed directions. A promising antenna architecture is based on an array antenna organized in interleaved subarrays (number of subarrays equal to the number of target beams M). Each subarray is having the periodic cell split in M sub-apertures. One of the M sub-apertures is occupied by a radiating element, the other M-1 slots are kept emptyto be used by the other M-1 interleaved subarrays. The dimension of the periodic cell is larger than one wavelength in order to create grating lobes exactly in the directions where the desired beams of the Scatterometer instrument are targeted. The array factor associated to the M phase centres of the M subarrays, when fed with identical phase value, creates a beam pointing at the boresight direction with radiative nulls positions coinciding with the grating lobes positions. Accordingly, when feeding the M inputs with thesame phase value a main beam in the boresight direction can be generated and the M-1 grating lobes can be cancelled by the radiative nulls. When feeding the M inputs with a linear phase in order to point the main beam exactly at one of the M possible targeted angles, the radiative nulls permit to cancel all the subarray pattern beams except the desired one. The M beams can be generated one atthe time, or simultaneously by adding a small beamforming MxM network. Possible values for M could be 3 or 5. To be noted also thatthecorresponding beams can be placed in the same azimuthal plane or not. This beamforming solution permits to reduce by a factor Mthe number of controls (phase shifters, direction couplers, amplifiers). As a consequence, a significant reduction in the cost and complexity of the entire instrument can be achieved. Reducing by a factor 3-5 the number of passive and active components in a Scatterometer instrument based on a phased array. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Instrument identification and requirements refinement. - Technology trade-off and down-selection. - Identification/optimization of most promising architectures. - Preliminary design of a baseline architecture and back-up architecture - Detailed design of a baseline architecture - Define preliminary manufacturing technique and prototype. - Definition of test and verification plan - Breadboard manufacturing and test - Results analysis and evaluation.
title: PHASED ARRAYS EXPLOITING GRATING LOBESFOR SCATTEROMETER INSTRUMENTS EXPRO PLUS

description: Objective: To identify and test European sourced conformal coatings to mitigate the risk of Sn whisker growth on COTS itemsDescription: Use of commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) components is becoming common in electronic units. These are typically finished with apure Sn finish which has been historically forbidden in space applications due to the risk of Sn whisker growth. The development ofSn whiskers can lead to short circuits within an electronic unit. This caused the loss of various telecommunication satellites in the early 2000s. The most promising method to mitigate this risk (without changing the plating of the components) is the use of conformal coatings. This activity assesses the ability of different conformal coatings to mitigate Sn whisker growth and investigate the influence of the coating process parameters (e.g. thickness, coverage of the application) on its efficacy. The impact of potential coating damage/defect will also be investigated, seeking to define workmanship criteria. Different test regimes for Sn whisker growthaccelerated testing shall be applied to comparing thermal cycling in ambient pressure, in vacuum and temperature/humidity aging. Different mission scenarios should also be considered (e.g. satellites, reusable systems and habitats). This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Literature search to review of test approaches for accelerated growth of Sn whiskers and to identify the conformal coatings to test. The selection of coatings shall include all classes of coatings most used in space with focus on European sourced ones (e.g. silicones, polyurethanes, acrylic, parylene). - Test plan definition. a) test vehicle design using elementary samples (Sn plated uCu sheets for example) with high susceptibility to grow whiskers. This is to allow a controlled application of the coatings. b) test matrix: application parameters to be assessed for each type of coating (thickness, application method.); type of defectsto be introduced (scratches, incomplete application..) c) multiple test regimes shall be applied on different sets of samples. testduration shall double the one defined in JESD201A. d) methodology to assess the growth of whiskers over time (Visual inspection, Scanning electron microscope, tomography...) - Testing and results assessment: classification of the coatings investigated and definition of minimum thickness and workmanship criteria for each coating. Potential future work would include testing of the coating application on EEE device or assemblies prone to grow Sn whiskers, as well as extended test durations.Deliverables: Prototype, Report
title: CHARACTERIZATION OF CONFORMAL COATINGS AS SN WHISKER RISK MITIGATION STRATEGY AT BOARD LEVEL - EXPRO+

description: ObjectivesTo develop a low frequency and low noise, 3 axis electric field probe, enabling direct ongroundverification by test fornext generation in-situ space plasma sensing missions and for missions with EMC sensitive payload integrated inside the spacecraft structure.DescriptionBackground and Context:Missions that are studying space plasma with wave instruments are imposing low frequency and low-level electric field requirements on the spacecraft in order to limit the unwanted radiated emission that could disturbthe instrument performance. In addition, other increasingly challenging and sensitive payloads also require more stringent control ofelectric fields at lower frequencies. Therefore, the on-ground verification of the electric field requirements driven by the payloads has paramount importance i.e. to confirm the presence of unintentional electric field interference originated from the spacecraftthat can jeopardize the instrument performance. Current electric field probes do not cover the needs of compact probing of low frequency and low noise radiated electric fields in which 3 axes and phase information is needed, in particular to characterise emissions close to units or even inside the spacecraft. By improving both the frequency range and thesensitivity, compact electric field probes could be utilised for improved verification and new applications that were not feasible before.Justification:The commercially available electric field probes are not suitable to capture the low frequencies and the low amplitudes, that are required for upcoming missions of Plasma Observatory, M-Matisse and New ATHENA or required by already flying missions like JUICE and Solar Orbiter.Description:The goal of the activity is to develop a triaxial field probe together with its conditioning unit with start frequency of 0.1 Hz or lower and sensitivity of 0.5 mV/m or lower up-to 200 kHz.An additional constraint for the field probe development is the size. The newly developed field probe shall allow to place minimum of 16 identical field probes around the unit under test at a distance closer than 0.25 m without interfering with each other.Moreover, the field probe needs to produce the field data along eachprincipal axes that can be processed with typical laboratory equipment like spectrum analyser, EMI receiver, digital oscilloscope, data acquisition unit, etc.Task list:- Identification of technology concepts and market research for state-of-the-art field probes in terms of frequency range, sensitivity and dynamic range- Evaluation of weak points of the existing field probes and identification of the critical components needed for the required improvements- Bread boarding of 3 axis sensor (e.g. optimize the type, sizeand shape of sensor) together with its conditioning unit (e.g. design a low noise read out chain including low noise amplifier) also considering constraints like size and cost- Validation tests and reportsDeliverables:- Documentation of the research- The bread board of the improved field probe together with its conditioning unit- Test reports and calibration data
title: COMPACT, EXTREME LOW FREQUENCY AND LOW NOISE ELECTRIC FIELD PROBE DEVELOPMENT EXPRO PLUS

description: The next European mission to land on Mars will be the Rosalind Franklin Rover mission, which relies on non-European input for key elements on the entry, descent and landing module. The rover will enter on a ballistic entry with no additional means for precision landing. Increase in mass and precision of future Mars surface missions in the coming decades is a strategic capability for Europe, as outlined in the Explore2040 strategy implementation roadmap. To achieve this ambition, Europe must advance developments of guided entry landers and their associated technologies, avoiding technological dead ends as the capability progresses. The Mars surface lander that is the subject of this study will target a high precision landing (2-7 km major axis), which could be the first in a roadmap of increasingly precise and heavier landers, eventually aiming for a pinpoint landing accuracy of a few 10s of metres.The objectives of this activity are to:- demonstrate the technical and programmatic feasibility (Phase A) of the first mission thatwill utilise an advanced entry descent and landing capability on Mars. Advanced entry,decent and landing (EDL) is defined as a capability toland on Mars with a higher level ofmass, guidance and precision than will have been achieved in Europe following the landingof Rosalind Franklin and includes fully European critical technologies.- assess a sustainable roadmap of technology developments suitable for increased precisionand mass landings on Mars in future missions, to avoid technological gaps and dead ends.
title: E4EX-006 MARS ADVANCED ENTRY, DESCENT AND LANDING CAPABILITY (MEDAL) - PHASE A

description: The proposed procurement covers the definition, deployment, operation and evolution of a ERSEO Element 1 Testbed, a sovereign, scalable, secure, capacity-building digital environment enabling the deployment and extensive testing of diverse vertical, resilience-oriented applications and enabling tools (i.e. the Proof-of-Concepts , PoCs).The Testbed is a key enabling element of the Element 1 Proof-of-Concept component providing a common, high-performance deployment and testing environment to maximise synergies and efficiency across PoCs. While the PoCs themselves will be procured under specific procurement actions and are outside the scope of the present procurement, ESA will ensure an optimised allocation and sharing of responsibilities between the Testbed contractor and the PoCsdevelopers, in line with their respective competences and roles.Key activities covered by the Procurement are: (1) Testbed architecture definition, (2) Testbed deployment, operation and evolution, (3) PoCs deployment and testing, (4) Validation of the set-up under representative conditions, (5) Production and maintenance of architecture blueprint and reference artefacts to support PoCs portability, scalability and procurement de-risking.The procurement will be conducted through a single Invitation to Tender with the objective of maximising synergies between the testbed architecture definition and the subsequent deployment of the testbed. description: Stepping Stone Missions are a new class of user driven Earth Observation missions designed to address gaps in the current EO ecosystem by delivering quality certified data and services tailored to environmental policy needs at European and global level. They build on and complement existing reference missions and infrastructures, while targeting observation domains and sampling requirements not adequately covered today. A key characteristic is their service oriented and commercially minded nature: missions are conceived from the outset to enable operational services, foster downstream applications, and evolve into scalable, privately operated constellations once their performance and utility have been demonstrated in orbit. The Stepping Stones activity focuses on conducting mission definition studies that mature candidate concepts up to a consolidated system baseline. This includes the parallel development of the space and ground segments, the definition of user oriented services, and the establishment of a robust business case demonstrating long term viability. The studies also encompass assessment of technical feasibility, verification and validation approaches, and readiness with respect to user needs, policy alignment, and commercial exploitation. Overall, the objective is to de risk and validate the end to end concepttechnical, service, and marketup to System Requirements Review level.
title: STEPPING STONE MISSION DEFINITION STUDY

description: Objective:To develop a complete ADHA solid-state mass-memory with compatible modules, usable either standalone orwith other ADHA-compatible hardware in ADHA units for Earth observation, exploration, science, andnavigation missions.Description:The ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) is a collaboration between ESA, European satellite primesand data handling equipment suppliers. It includes the definition of an architecture for data handling unitsbased on standard module functions. A standard module procurementflow has been defined, as well as astandardized backplane connector and electrical interfaces. This allows independent developmentofinteroperable modules that can be connected in ADHA units.This activity aims to develop ADHA solid-state mass-memory (MM) modules, based on ADHA-compatiblehardware modules. The development will follow the standard requirements for the development of ADHAmodules.The mass-memory module design will be fully compliant to the ADHA generic specification for mass-memorymodules. The developmentwill include the development of the mass-memory software (including support forfile-based operations, and CFDP Class-1 and Class-2). The developed ADHA mass memory module willsupport high-speed data reception and transfers, featuring a scalable architecture to meet the demands offuture ESA missions in earth observation, science, exploration, and navigation, as well as commercialmissions. Utilizing state-of-the-art processing, memory storage and interconnect technologies, this new massmemoryshall offer superior integration, data storage volume and processing performance compared toprevious generations. These advancements will also enable the implementation of sophisticated functionssuch as artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) algorithms for on-board data processing.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Detailed module requirements analysis, based on the existing ADHA specification documents, including theADHA generic mass-memory module specification.- ADHA mass memory module architectural design and trade-off of key components.- Engineering model (EM) design, including electrical, mechanical, thermal, FPGA design and software.- Engineering model (EM) manufacturing and EGSE procurement.- Engineering model (EM) validation campaign, including integration in anADHA unit rack.- Data-handling and storage demonstration, including performance benchmarks.NOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

description: ObjectivesTo develop an integrity concept leveraging Position, Velocity and Time (PVT) assurance solutions for safety critical applications.DescriptionSafety critical applications rely on integrity concepts based on protection levels and alerting schemes to bound the position error in nominal and failure scenarios under a given integrity risk. This allows estimating the worst-case user position systematically taking into account potential feared events. Similar integrity concepts and list of feared events can be developed considering the potential presence of intentional GNSS signal impairments.The Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) providers are implementing mechanism in order to protect the users from security threats such as spoofing. For instance, Galileo will provide both navigation message authentication (NMA) and ranging authentication (Commercial Service Authentication [CAS]). Therefore, the user integrity concepts will have to be expanded to define the impact of intentional interference, to specify the related feared events, and to consider the barriers provided by PVT assurance solutions.This activity aims at exploring technological enablers, algorithms and concepts for future positioning integrity concepts, which would enable safe and secure operations even in the presence of potential intentional impairments. It will investigate the contribution to the overall safety and trustworthiness provided by GNSS-based PVT assurance. Moreover, attention will be given to demonstrating that the overall target integrity can be achieved by different positioning solutions and PVT assurance techniques.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- State-of-the-art survey of integrity concepts for PVT, of PVT assurance services, and of anti-spoofing techniques,- Development of innovative security-aware concepts,- Performance assessment of the integrity concepts,- Roadmap for standardization.DeliverablesReport, Software

description: This activity focuses on designing and optimizing Position, Velocity, and Time (PVT) engines specifically for LEO-based PNT systems. It aims to exploit the unique measurement diversity offered by LEO satellites, such as multipath whitening, Doppler utilization, and rapid LOS/NLOS transitions. Two approaches will be developed and compared: a conventional Kalman filter-based design and an AI/ML-based design to handle unexpected LEO measurement behaviours. The study will include state-of-the-art review, algorithm development, and benchmarking against traditional MEO GNSS-based engines. Field measurement campaigns will validate performance and inform a roadmap for commercialization. For more info, visit https://navisp.esa.int/opportunity
title: NAVISP-EL1-124-OPTIMISATION OF PVT ENGINES FOR LEO MEASUREMENT DIVERSITY - EXPRO+

description: General DescriptionThis activity explores the application of Approximate Computing (AxC) techniques to GNSS signal processing for reducing power consumption while maintaining acceptable accuracy. It focuses on implementing AxC in acquisition, tracking, and PVT stages of GNSS receivers. The study will identify suitable AxC methods, develop a prototype receiver supporting both exact and approximate modes, and evaluate performance in terms of power efficiency, accuracy, and correlation degradation. Test campaigns will use live and replayed GNSS data from various environments to validate the concept. For more info, visit https://navisp.esa.int/opportunity

description: Activity 2B addresses Phase B of the Alpstar Federation Layer, aiming to consolidate requirements, architecture, and prototype validation for a federated, multi stakeholder space system. Building on the MRD 2.0, this phase will define and specify all functional, technical, and security requirements of the Federation Layer, including secure interfaces with commercial service providers and Alpstar Nodes via unidirectional "diode" connections.The activity encompasses the full design of the Alpstar system architecture and the development and demonstration of a User Ground Segment prototype. Comprehensive specifications will be produced for all major Federation Layer components, ensuring interoperability, security, and scalability across federated participants.The procurement also includes the acquisition of a minimum of three months of satellite data, necessary to support validation and testing of the Ground Segment prototype under operationally representative conditions.A key deliverable of this phase is a User Ground Segment prototype featuring:A role based user interface, enabling differentiated access and operational views.An initial implementation of the Digital Governance Agent (DGA), enforcing a first set of provisional federation rules and acting as the central mission management and planning capability.The Alpstar Federated Layer shall integrate the following core functionalities:Digital Governance Agent (DGA)for federation rule enforcement and central mission managementSecure Data Pooling Service for controlled dissemination of observation resultsFederated Ledger to record and audit transactionsStandardised APIs interfacing with Nodes (FOS and PDGS)Federated Data Lake hosted in a cloud environmentVirtual Constellation Management for coordinated asset utilisationFederated CatalogueCross federation taskingNATO FMN / Joint ISR tasking interfaces routed to AlpstarRole based user interfaceFederation dashboard for operational and governance oversightWith a target duration of 12 months, the expected outcomes of Activity 2B include:Complete specifications of the Federation LayerDefinition of the Federation Layer architectureRough Order of Magnitude (ROM)cost estimate for implementationIdentification of the industrial consortiumDevelopment plan and integrated scheduleDemonstration of the User Ground Segment prototypeThis phase will provide the technical, architectural, and organisational foundations required to progress Alpstar toward a fully operational, secure, and governed federated space capability.

description: Objective: To develop the GNC architecture and algorithms required to enable precise landing of launcher stages / booster with highthrust-to-weight ratio via accurate hover-slam maneuvering.Description: Recent developments in reusable launch systems have demonstrated the operational and economic advantages of recovering and reusing first-stage boosters and upper stages. However, the current state-of-the-art is limited to a small number of operators, and many of the underlying technologies, including GNC for precision propulsive landing of high thrust-to-weight ratio vehicles, remain at low TRL, in particular in Europe. Achieving pinpoint landing ischallenging due to restrictive throttling constraints and to tight dynamical couplings where there is no room for error: the required Thrust Vector Control (TVC) deflections are large and so is the drift they induce, the controllability offered by fins is limiteddue to the low velocities, and the vehicle is operating under uncertain conditions stemming from interactions such as plume impingement and ground effect. This activity will tackle these challenges by advancing GNC technologies for propulsive stages descent, trajectory shaping, terminal landing maneuvers and autonomous control. The following key enabling GNC functions will be developed as part of the study: - Descent Guidance Algorithms - Navigation filters based on multiple sensors fusion (e.g. altimeters, multiple IMUs,multiple GNSS antennas and receivers, strain gauges) - Control strategies and multiple-actuation architectures (TVC, fins, thrusters) - Autonomy functions (real-time decision-making, contingency handling, failure detection) The aims at investigating candidate GNCarchitectures and algorithms suitable for landing scenarios, considering as a minimum boosters and upper stages landing. This is critical to enable cost-effective and robust European solutions for reusable launchers in future missions. This activity encompassesthe following tasks: - Identify representative mission scenarios for vertical propulsive landing (hover-slam manoeuvre) - Define mission and system-level requirements for each scenario and vehicle - Develop modular GNC architectures - Model environmental dynamics (gravity, aerodynamics, wind) and vehicle dynamics (multi-body kinematics, flexible structures, sloshing) - Integrate GNC algorithms in a high-fidelity 6-DOF simulation framework - Perform trade studies on actuators and sensors, including sensitivity and robustness analysis - Validation and verification campaign of the selected GNC architectures and algorithms, including an evaluation of performance - Study synthesis and recommendations for a technology roadmap to increase TRL
title: GNC TECHNOLOGIES FOR PRECISE LANDING OF LAUNCHER STAGE AND BOOSTER - EXPRO PLUS

description: Objective:To design, develop, implement, test and verify secure reconfigurable technologies needed to support softwaredefined satellites.Description:Europe's first commercial satellite capable of being completely reprogrammed while in space are already incommercial use. Such satellites offer unprecedented mission reconfiguration capacity and capabilities(including but not limited to beams reshaping and redirection). In addition, in-flight re-programmabilitycapabilities that will enable avionic platforms to support many missions are also considered. The availability ofsystem-on-chip, powerful micro-controllers and reprogrammable Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA)enables a high-level of flexibility while improving the performance of avionic systems.However, all these software defined capabilities and flexibility require to be managed and implemented in asecure way, to ensure that cannot be exploitedby potential attackers to compromise the confidentiality,integrity or availability of the provided services, of the software defined capabilities and of the platform itself.Security measures, including access controls, cryptographic based authentication, software authenticityprotection using digital signatures or other suitable technology, secure booting based on root of trust, user /operator / management segregation, and other, must be implemented.This activity is divided in phases and encompasses the following tasks:Phase 1 (budget: 500 k, duration: 8 months):- Asses the state of the art of software defined satellites technologies and architectures.- Security assessment of the risks of using these technologies and architectures, identification and assessmentof securitytechnologies that can be used to mitigate these risks; identification of suitable products (software /hardware) implementing thesesecurity technologies.- Design a complete secure reconfigurable software defined satellite using the identified security technologiesto address the security risks.- Proof-of-concept development of selected functionalities, demonstration and testing.Phase 2 (budget: 1,500 k, duration: 16 months):- Develop the technologies that will be used for securing the configuration and authenticity of software definedsatellites.- Implement an end-to-end secure reconfigurable software defined satellite.- Test, verify and demonstrate end-to-end secure reconfigurable software defined satellite.
title: SECURE RECONFIGURABLE SOFTWARE DEFINED SATELLITES - EXPRO+

description: Objective: To develop a small three-rack-unit version of the Advanced Power Architecture (APA) with aim of having a highly compact architecture fit for small missions.Description: The Advanced Power Architecture (APA) is being designed for general ESA mission /medium scale platform but is not addressing smaller mission needs. This activity aims at developing the APA concept in a three-rack-unit (3U) version; this footprint would be suitable for smaller satellites up to 500 kg. The activity targets to investigate the miniaturisation of the already identified functions by integrating novel technologies such as digital control and Gallium Nitride High-Electron Mobility transistor (GaN HEM FET). The Advanced Data Handling Architecture (ADHA) has already a 3U version which, if coupled with a 3U version of the APA, it would enable a single frame for a very compact avionics system. In fact, the APA will provide the input power interface, the TM/TC interface, the internal power rails and the internal communication bus. Thus, any platform function not needing internal high speed data communication buses could fit perfectly in the 3U APA. For instance, the solar array drive function or any motor drive function, propulsion valves drive functions, thermal control, etc. The activity targets to enhance industrialisation of power units for mid-size satellites by having the full power system functionality integrated in one unit. If deemed adequate for the application, a cost-effective solution could be available by having the components as COTS. A strong focus on manufacturability and industrialisation will be done, focusing on automatic manufacturing, planar transformers, SMD components, etc. This activity focuses on the development of the Solar Array Regulator (SAR) module with miniaturised DC/DC converter and on the Solar Array Drive Electronics (SADE) demonstrating the applicability of the concept to the entire avionics functions. These will be the firstbuilding blocks for the development of the complete functionality. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Converter andfilter size reduction thanks to the use of HEM FET (GaN) - Inclusion of the Solar Array Drive Electronics to embed all potential EPS need - Design and manufacturing of a breadboard - Test of the breadboard - Validation and verification - Way forward for industrialization
title: 3U VERSION OF THE ADVANCED POWER ARCHITECTURE (APA) - EXPRO+

description: Objective: To develop a memory array based on M2 PCIe NAND flash memory Solid State Drives modules and characterise the radiation effects and possible mitigation methods at software and hardware levels.Description: High density Mass storage solutions based on NAND flash memory Solid State Drives (SSD) are widely used in data server applications and present a great opportunity for space applications. However, their reliability and their tolerance to radiation-induced effects have not been evaluated so far. M2 PCI ExpressNon-Volatile Memory (NVM) storage drives are now commonly used System on Module (SoM) devices, similar in size to Double Dada Rate (DDR) memory modules used in personal computers, and capable of storing over 1TB of data. These SoMs incorporate advanced Error Detection and Correction (EDAC) systems to manage the frequent occurrence of bad blocks and bits in 3D NAND Flash Memories. These devicescan be used in a Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) due to Peripheral Component Interconnect Express (PCIe) interface. Thecombination of powerful EDAC and the hot redundancy of RAID is beneficial for addressing the anticipated radiation effects and wearout in NAND Flash memories when used in Space. The non-volatile nature of these memories helps preventing data loss during power cycling to recover Single Event Functional Interrupts (SEFI) in the control electronics. Additionally, these storage drives are currently used in high-speed computation nodes where radiation effects caused by neutrons and alpha particles are a concern. The PCIe interface is widely supported in commercial processors and FPGAs, and will be featured in the next generation of space-graded processorsand FPGAs. The PCIe interface targets to enable the use of very high density, compact, non-volatile memories modules, for the nextgeneration platform and payload units (OBCs, solid state mass memories, ICUs, etc). This proposal aims to develop a RAID array controlled by a European processor or FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Arrays), using various M2 PCIe NVMe SSD modules. This setup enables the assessment of feasibility and reliability concerning radiation and wear out effects, paving the way for a new concept of extremelyhigh-density data storage for space applications. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Selection of several candidateM2 PCIe SSD devices from different manufacturers. - Development of a Single Event Effect (SEE) test setup for SSD drives using thePCIe compatible European processor / FPGA in RAID configuration. - Proton and heavy ion SEE testing- Assessment of the test results and proposal of further mitigation techniques if needed.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs).  For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses
title: M2 PCIE NVME SOLID STATE DRIVES FOR FUTURE MASS STORAGE SOLUTIONS EXPRO+

description: Objective: To develop high-density, high-data-rate mezzanine connectors for parallel board integration, ensuring reliable high-speed signal transmission and optimized space efficiency.Description: The increasing modularity of onboard digital processing units, such as those based on the Advanced Data Handling Architecture (ADHA), is driving demand for mezzanine-based designs that allow for mission-specific customisation of front-panel interfaces (e.g., SpW, SpFi, Ethernet, RF ADC/DAC, and memory). These mezzanine boards avoid redesigning complex main PCBs built around high-performance FPGAs and processors, enabling faster iteration and mission tailoring. However, the lack of space-qualified mezzanine connectors that meet mechanical, electrical, and environmental requirements presents a major integration barrier. In the absence of suitable solutions, some suppliers resort to adapting backplane connectors, whichare not optimised for mezzanine use and create challenges in mechanical layout and signal integrity. Commercial mezzanine connectors(COTS) similarly fall short of the standards needed for thermal, outgassing, and reliability performance in space. This activity supports the European strategic goal to develop modular platform architectures for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites, particularly in the mid-size class (100-500 kg, 200 W to 2 kW), by 2028. A new mezzanine connector is aimed to be developed to enable high-speed, high-density signal routing with robust mechanical integration and compliance with space environmental constraints. The design targetsto meet the following key requirements: - Support SerDes (Serialiser/Deserialise) data rates =10 Gbit/s per lane (target: 16.3 Gbit/s; scalable to 30-40 Gbit/s for next-gen FPGAs); - Total pin count around 150-200, with subsets for SerDes, Low-Voltage Differential Signaling (LVDS) (hundreds of Mbit/s), etc.; - Mechanical compatibility with 6HP-height 3U ADHA modules for front-panel interfacing.This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Literature review and market survey of mezzanine/backplane connector technologies,including COTS and qualification status; - Technology and process review to identify promising connector concepts and materials, based on supplier constraints; - Design and prototyping of a new connector optimised for space use in 3U systems; - Electrical characterisation up to 40 Gbit/s/lane and environmental qualification (vibration, thermal cycling, endurance with continuity monitoring);- Identification of limitations, proposed improvements, and roadmap toward space qualification, including a standardisation strategy.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). description: Objective: To manufacture a detector with sensitivity up to 10 um wavelength and perform its detailed performance assessment at operating temperatures down to 40 K.Description: The Near Earth Object Mission in the Infra-Red (NEOMIR hereafter) aims to overcome most of the issues encountered previously with respect to NEO (Near Earth Object) detection by regularly scanning an area not accessible by ground or other space-based NEO surveys. NEOMIR will be capable of detecting and characterizing new NEOs and - in the worst case of an imminent impactor - serve as an early warning system. The noise contribution from the detector and instrument on NEOMIR must be minimised to ensure the signal from small or distant NEOs is not lost into the background noise. These requirements drive the detector's operating temperature down towards 40 K and necessitate careful engineering of its detection layer. Within this activity,test samples of suitable detection layers will be manufactured and hybridised to readout circuits. These will be characterised downto 40 K operating temperature, assessing their performance in conditions close to those expected in NEOMIR. Where applicable, the characterisation will provide statistics on the spatial and temporal variability of device performance parameters including quantum efficiency, dark current, linearity and crosstalk. The measured performance will be provided to inform mission-level performance simulations and planning of calibration routines. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Prototype device design and manufacturing. - Test planning and test system design. - Test system assembly and commissioning. - Test campaign. - Performance assessment and conclusionsDeliverables: Prototype, ReportProcurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity)of non-primes (incl. description: The objective of this activity is to develop a physically-based framework that describes and simulates the temporal variation and fluctuations of the scattered SAR signal induced by vegetation. To achieve this, the Contractor shall define such framework and its architecture, along with the necessary interfaces, the different components, and the expected inputs and outputs, focusing on representing the scattering of SAR signals by vegetated land surfaces. The framework shall be modular and applicable to a wide range of present and future missions and scenarios, and shall allow the use and intercomparison of different modelling approaches. It shall be designed to:1.           cover multiple frequencies of the incident signal, with a focus on C-band and L-band as a minimum2.    accommodate the simulations of the effects of several categories of vegetation, e.g. from forests to agricultural fields3.      capture different temporal scales of the signal evolution in the simulations, that could range for example from seconds to days4.           Output the complex scattered field, which can then be used for subsequent performance analysisFurther, the Contractor shall develop the models that go into the framework and validate them using existing spaceborne, airborne and on-ground datasetswhen available. The models shall be physically-based, describe the scattering mechanisms with sufficient accuracy, and shall be parameterized and validated using experimental observations. The validation shall be focused on a limited number of scenarios, that must be representative of candidate SAR missions (like Hydroterra+) and planned SAR missions (e.g. ROSE-L). After implementation and validation, the Contractor shall analyse the outputs of the simulations and conduct sensitivity analyses, to understand and characterize the impact of vegetation on both amplitude and phase of the output observations, and its effect on the Single Look Complex (SLC) and interferometric products.
title: A PHYSICALLY-BASED MULTI-TIMESCALE MODELLING FRAMEWORK OF DYNAMIC VEGETATION SIGNALS FOR SAR - EXPRO PLUS
