description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to investigate mission concepts for entanglement distribution QUAntum SpAce netwoRk (QUASAR) in the context ofQuantum Information Networks. The aim is to define preliminary requirements of the in-orbit-experiment, involving a space segment and at least twodistant ground stations, required to verify entanglement distribution from space.TargetedImprovements:The targeted improvement is to mature the quantum payload concept definition and mission requirement, to improve the viability of the in-orbitexperiment of satellite entanglement distribution with the current and near-future technology.Description: The development of Quantum Information Networks (QIN) is rapidly increasing, driven largely by the expansion of terrestrial fibre networks. However,long distance quantum communication remains fundamentally constrained by fibre losses. To overcome this limitation, the integration of a space segmentis essential. A critical step towards this integration is the execution of an in-orbit experimentto validate space-to-ground entanglement distribution. Thismission would represent a major milestone in demonstrating the satellites' role in the expansion of Quantum Information Networks.The proposed activity aims to prove the technical feasibility of space-based QIN. Consequently, this would strengthen the market potential by confirmingsatellite-to-ground entanglement distribution capabilities. The main tasks of this activity will: identifying the critical elements involved in the space and ground segments (for technical and economic suitability); exploring the various possible system concepts by modelling to determine possibilities, characteristics or the criticality of certain elements; comparing these concepts against the needs, to determine levels of uncertainty andrisk; estimating the technical and industrial feasibility; identifying, for each possible system concept, the constraints relating to costs, schedules, organisation, utilisation (operations, implementation,maintenance), production and disposal, as well as the estimated margins in relation to the targets.
title: EXPLORING MISSION CONCEPTS FOR QUANTUM SPACE NETWORK (QUASAR) DEMONSTRATOR (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3H.012) - EXPRO+

description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop the required digital processing hardware needed for an optical transceiver supporting multiple optical waveformsat different data rates on a single wavelength.TargetedImprovements:Provide a European solution for a flexible space optical communication coherent modem capable of reaching 100 Gbps.Description: Multiple optical transceivers are being proposed and developed by emerging suppliers in Europe. These transceivers are either already available for theterrestrial market or are currently under development for satellite applications. Some suppliers aim for less complex products, targeting 2.5 Gbps links,while some others utilise advanced optical modulation formats capable of achieving data rates beyond 100 Gbps. Consequently, the creation of an in-orbitreconfigurable transceiver is crucial to addressing different needs from back-bone network satellites and customer satellites connecting to such satellitenetworks. Flexibility in wavefront and optical interfaces will enable grater interoperability and allow flexible services to be provided by the existing andfuture European and international satellites. This activity will develop the real-time digital processing hardware of a flexible digital coherent opticaltransceiver. The digital processing module is typically composed of several chiplets including a flexible chiplet (DSP, FEC, turbulence mitigation,mod/demod), a SERDES chiplet and analogue/digital converter chiplets (TIA/Drivers, ADC/DAC). The key aspects to be considered are limited size, weightand power consumption while enabling throughput as high as 100 Gbps. Flexibility in waveform as well as client-side interfaces is required.The main engineering tasks include:- Identification of the individual components and connection interfaces (hardware and software).- Design of the transceiver architecture and development of a virtual prototype (e.g. formal verification).- Implementation of a transceiver scaled EM.
title: FLEXIBLE DIGITAL COHERENT OPTICAL MODULE FOR OPTICAL COMMUNICATION (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5H.016)

description: The objective of the activity is to assess the suitability of the latest generation of COTS Digital Coherent Optical (DCO) modules for optical intersatelliteand cross-atmospheric links.TargetedImprovements:Enabling optical inter satellite links (OISLs) with adata rate four times higher than previously demonstrated. Improving the efficiency of transceivers(energy/bit).Description: The current generation of coherent transceivers Digital Coherent Optical (DCO) modules tested and implemented in current laser communication terminalsallow data rates from 100 to 200 Gbps. However, the latest generation of COTS DCO (fibre networks) extends this range to 800 Gbps, leveraging severaltechnological advancements, in a new (smaller) form factor.This activity will analyse and assess the performance and the environmental suitability of the COTS transceivers for their potential use, as well as theadvantages coming from using those devices in space. Relevant performance metrics are, for example, the bit error rate vs. received power, the receiversensitivity, and the synchronisation and re-synchronisation capability (during acquisition, tracking and operation). description: Objective: To develop and mature architectures for photon counting pixelated detectors in the visible range.Description: The trend of improving readout noise performance has approached the threshold where high performance imaging detectors can count the number of photoelectrons collected in each sampling period. This ultimate performance limit allows the contribution of readout noise to be entirely removed, eliminating a contribution to the signal to noise budget of instruments. In this activity, pixel architectures able to reach photon counting sensitivity in the 400-800 nm wavelength range are being explored. The assessment targets large focal plane arrays operating at high photon flux rates typical of Earth Observation applications. Other aspects such as susceptibility to thespace radiation environment and feasibility of manufacture within current CMOS imaging fabrication processes are considered. description: To minimise salt loss, to optimise salt stability and to enable salt regeneration/purification for themolten salt electrolysis process.DescriptionThe Fray Farthing Chen (FFC) Cambridge process and similar Molten Salt Electrolysis (MSE)processes, including the Regolith to OXYgen and Metals Conversion (ROXY) process, are potentialgame changing approaches to making resources available in alunar environment, i.e. the oxygenand metals which are chemically bound to lunar and planetary regolith/ bedrock.To operate an MSE based In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) process on planetary surfaces, withthe minimum need of resupply of consumables, the salt/electrolyte recovery, stability andregeneration are of utmost importance for the sustainability of the in-situ process.To successfully apply this process for ISRU, essential aspects to be understood include: the saltrecovery from the porous reduced feed stockmaterial, as well as the salt regeneration/purificationfrom processing immanent contaminants, and from degradation products. description: Objective: To develop an ultra-low power, Mixed Signal Microcontroller (MCU) for hibernation control for Avionics units.Description: Planetary and deep space missions necessitate a hibernation controller that can operate reliably at low power for extended periods, even under extreme temperature variations. This controller is essential for managing the wake-up and shut-down processes of avionics during planetary nights and deep space travel, ensuring the spacecraft's survival and functionality throughout the mission. Recent advancements in semiconductor technology and manufacturing have significantly reduced the power consumption of digital logic andprocessors, while also expanding their operating temperature range to include cryogenic levels. These developments are particularlyrelevant for ensuring the reliable operation of Mixed Signal Microcontrollers (MCUs) across a wide temperature spectrum at ultra-low power levels. MCUs, commonly used as primary processing units in control applications and on-board computers, can be equipped withsmall dedicated circuits to enter hibernation mode and wake up periodically for operational tasks or in response to sensor alarms. This results in power consumption as low as 10 nA. An MCU with such capabilities would be ideal for the hibernation controller in avionics subsystems, offering significant advantages over discrete solutions with limited functionality and higher power consumption. Theactivity includes a survey of available space-grade MCUs to identify a suitable candidate for managing the hibernation and control of the start-up and shut-down processes of avionics electronics. The final selection is based on a thorough analysis and environmental testing of the identified MCU. Integrating a small, ultra-low power, reliable clock and monitoring alarm circuit are used to upgrade the selected MCU to serve as a hibernation controller for planetary and deep space missions. The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Use case determination - Analysis, thermal environmental testing and selection of space grade MCUs for hibernation controller functions - Evaluation of the MCU technology for the implementation of an ultra-low power clock and monitoring alarm circuit - Design of the ultra low-power hibernation clock and monitoring alarm function - Incorporation of the hibernation clock and monitoring alarm into the MCU - Manufacturing of the hibernation MCU (h-MCU) - Thermal environmental testing of the h-MCU - Evaluation of MCU and hibernation functions - Demonstration of an h-MCU module for incorporation into space avionic systems.ProcurementPolicy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). description: Objective: To define and assess the feasibility of a digitally controlled, highly efficient and compact High-Power Amplifiers in L-band / C-band for PNT applications.Description: With the increased demand for navigation services, the number of signal componentstransmitted by a GNSS satellite has increased. Since constant envelope multiplexing schemes are not suitable (or inefficient) with ahigh number of signal components, modern GNSS systems generate signals with high PAPR (Peak to average Power Ratio). DC power efficiency is critical for high power amplifiers (HPA) transmitting signals with high PAPR. In the last decades several HPA architectureshave been investigated to solve this limitation. Among those, the category of polar transmitters such as Envelope Tracking (ET) andEnvelope Elimination and Restoration (EER) stand out for high efficiency and excellent thermal management of the transistors. Conversely, they showed major challenges such as high complexity and difficult implementation with wideband signals. Given the narrowbandnature of Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) signals, polar transmitters are a good candidate for PNT applications. The challenge of analogue envelope reconstruction can be overcome by a digital modulator, leveraging recent advances in digital technologies. Atthe same time, evolution of PNT services is moving beyond L-band, targeting C-band or other frequency bands with larger bandwidths,where there is no example of dedicated HPAs for navigation. This activity will investigate amplifier design solutions to address high PAPR narrow band, as well as medium PAPR broadband signal configurations. The amplifiers will include digital predistortion, to achieve high-quality PNT signal performance, and compact designs to target advanced payload architectures. The selected designs willbe demonstrated through the development and testing of elegant breadboards (EBB) This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition of the operational scenarios and end-to-end user requirements associated. - Literature review, oriented at the latest developments in ET and polar transmitters in general, in analogue and in digital domain, as well as in broadband HPA solutions - Trade-off and down-selection of the most promising technologies based on the survey and preliminary high-level studies - Breadboards detailed design, and analysis and preparation of manufacturing plan and test plan - Breadboards manufacturing and test - Critical analysis of the results obtained and future roadmap.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). description: Objective: To develop a E-/W-band traveling wave tube slow-wave structure breadboard capable of delivering 100 W of output power.Description: The millimetre wave domain is also known as the extremely high-frequency (EHF) spectrum ranges from 30 to 300 GHz. Early works on atmospheric propagation in EHF evidenced encouraging future usage for satellite communications. The allocated W-band for satellite services (71-76 GHz and 81-86 GHz) potentially provides a favourable attenuation window due to low oxygen absorption. The exploitation of W-band may offer broad bandwidths for high data rate information transfer. Hence the development of the high power amplifiers is a critical building block that acts as an enabler to exploit this frequency band for satellite telecommunications. Currently, solid state power amplifiers cover this frequency band, but with output powers significantly lower than 100 W and very low efficiency. A traveling wave tube amplifier (TWTA) solution offers better performance in terms of output power and efficiency. This activity aims at developing a traveling wave tube slow-wave structure in W-band, capable of delivering 100 W of output power. As a result of the validation of this key building block, European industry will gain crucial knowledge and pass a first important milestoneon their way to design and manufacture full TWTs in this frequency band. At present, no W-band space TWTs are available in Europe. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Design a traveling wave tube slow-wave structure in W-band, capable of delivering 100 W of output power - Manufacturing of a breadboard - Testing and validation of a breadboardDeliverables: Breadboard, Report
title: DEVELOPMENT OF E-/W-BAND SLOW WAVE STRUCTURE BREAD BOARDS FOR HIGH POWER TWTS EXPRO+
